summaries.apostolic-decree: The Apostolic Decree is the binding decision issued by the Jerusalem Council in Acts 15:19-29, ruling that Gentile converts need not be circumcised or come under the Mosaic…
summaries.apostolic-hermeneutic: The Apostolic Hermeneutic is the interpretive method modeled by the apostles in their use of the Old Testament throughout the New.
summaries.apostolic: Apostolic means of, from, or in continuity with the original apostles — their teaching, authority, mission, and example.
summaries.apostolicity: The mark of the true Church by which it remains anchored to the faith once delivered through the apostles of Jesus Christ.
summaries.appointed: In Scripture, to be appointed is to be set apart by divine determination for a specific purpose, time, or role.
summaries.approbation: The formal, tested approval of God — His declaration that a person, work, or offering has been examined and found worthy. Biblical approbation is never cheap;
summaries.appropriation: In biblical theology, appropriation is the act of personally receiving and making one's own the benefits of Christ's atonement through faith.
summaries.aquila: Aquila was a Jewish man from Pontus expelled from Rome under Emperor Claudius' edict (Acts 18:2).
summaries.aquinas: Thomas Aquinas (1225-1274) was the Dominican friar whose Summa Theologica remains the dominant medieval synthesis of theology and philosophy.
summaries.ararat: Ararat is the mountainous region — in modern eastern Turkey near the Armenian border — where Noah’s ark came to rest after the Flood (Genesis 8:4).
summaries.archangel: The highest rank in the angelic hierarchy; in Scripture, explicitly named only once (Jude 9, of Michael).
summaries.archippus: A minister of the gospel in Colossae, almost certainly the son of Philemon and Apphia (Phlm 2 calls him our fellowsoldier).
summaries.argument-from-conscience: The Argument from Conscience holds that the universal moral conscience — the felt sense of this is right; that is wrong —
summaries.argument-from-design: The Argument from Design (also called the Teleological Argument) infers the existence of an intelligent Designer from the order, complexity, and apparent purpose observed in nature.
summaries.argument-from-meaning: The Argument from Meaning holds that the universal human longing for meaning — for ultimate purpose, for life that matters —
summaries.argument-from-reason: The Argument from Reason holds that human rational thought cannot have arisen from purely non-rational physical causes.
summaries.arianism: Arianism is the most famous and most durable Christological heresy in church history. Arius taught that "there was a time when the Son was not" —
summaries.arise: To arise is to stand up, get up, rise — and Scripture loads the verb in four directions. First, the imperative of urgent obedience: "Arise, get thee to Nineveh" (Jonah 1:2);
summaries.aristarchus: Aristarchus was a Thessalonian Macedonian believer who shared so much of Paul’s ministry that he appears at three major junctures.
summaries.ark-noah: The three-decked wooden vessel God commanded Noah to build for the salvation of his household and the animals during the deluge (Gen 6);
summaries.ark: The word "ark" covers two distinct sacred objects in Scripture: (1) Noah's Ark —
summaries.arm-biblical: "The arm of the LORD" is one of Scripture's most common images of divine saving power. "You with your mighty arm redeemed your people" (Ps 77:15).
summaries.arm: The upper limb; in Scripture, the most-used metaphor for divine strength. Israel was redeemed from Egypt with a stretched out arm (Deut 5:15);
summaries.armageddon: Armageddon appears only once by name in Scripture: Revelation 16:16.
summaries.arminianism: Arminianism is a theological system that elevates the role of human free will in salvation, teaching that God's election is conditional upon foreseen faith, that Christ's…
summaries.armor-of-god: Paul's metaphor in Ephesians 6:11-17 of the saint's spiritual-warfare equipment.
summaries.armor: The armor of God (Ephesians 6:11–17) is the complete spiritual equipment provided by God for the believer engaged in cosmic warfare against "the rulers, against the authorities,…
summaries.arrogant: Claiming more for oneself than is one's due; the heart-disposition that exalts the self beyond what reality warrants. Greek alazon (boaster, braggart).
summaries.arrow: The arrow is a versatile biblical metaphor. God Himself is a warrior whose arrows pierce the wicked: "If a man does not repent, God will whet his sword;
summaries.artisan: An artisan is a practitioner of a trained, skilled trade — the carpenter, mason, smith, weaver, embroiderer. Scripture honors them by name.
summaries.asaph: Asaph was the chief of the Levitical worship leaders appointed by David for tabernacle and (later) temple service (1 Chronicles 16:4-7, 37; 25:1-2).
summaries.ascend: To ascend is to go up — and Scripture loads the verb with theological weight.
summaries.ascending-jerusalem: Ascending to Jerusalem is the Hebrew idiom aliyah (going up): regardless of which direction one approaches from, one always ascends to Jerusalem because it is the city on the hill.
summaries.ascension-day: The Christian observance forty days after Easter commemorating Christ's bodily ascension from the Mount of Olives to the Father's right hand.
summaries.ascension-doctrine: The Ascension is the doctrinal fact that forty days after His resurrection, the Lord Jesus, in His glorified human body, was visibly taken up into heaven from the disciples’ sight…
summaries.ascension-event: The Ascension is one of the most important events in the life of Christ, but also one of the most neglected in modern evangelical teaching.

summaries.ascension-theology: The ascension of Christ is the historical event in which the risen Jesus was taken up bodily into heaven and seated at the right hand of the Father.
summaries.ascension: The bodily, visible, and glorious ascent of the risen Lord Jesus Christ to the right hand of the Father forty days after His resurrection (Acts 1:9–11).
summaries.asceticism: Asceticism, in its biblical form, is the disciplined denial of the body's appetites in service of spiritual alertness and conformity to Christ.
summaries.ascribe: To ascribe is to attribute, give credit to — and in Scripture it is the worship-verb par excellence. "Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name;

summaries.ash-heap: Job 2:8's location of Job's deepest suffering: "And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.
summaries.asham-offering: The asham (אָשָׁם) is the Mosaic trespass or guilt offering, prescribed in Leviticus 5:14-19 and 6:1-7 for sins requiring restitution —
summaries.ashdod: One of the five great Philistine cities (the Pentapolis: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Gath, Ekron), on the southern coastal plain of Canaan.
summaries.asherah-pole: The Asherah pole (Hebrew asherah, rendered "grove" in the KJV) was the carved wooden cult-symbol of the Canaanite mother-goddess Asherah, consort of El and rival to YHWH.
summaries.ashes: Ashes are the residue of what has burned — Scripture’s emblem of repentance, mourning, and consumed flesh yielded to God.
summaries.ashkelon: One of the five great Philistine cities (the Pentapolis: Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod, Gath, Ekron), an ancient seaport on the Mediterranean coast about ten miles north of Gaza.
summaries.ask-and-receive: Christ's threefold promise about prayer: "Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth;
summaries.assembly: The assembly in Scripture is the covenant people of God gathered in his presence for worship, instruction, and corporate action.
summaries.assimilation: Scripture presents a complex picture of assimilation. Israel was commanded to remain distinct from the surrounding nations — "You shall not do as they do in the land of Egypt...
summaries.assurance-pardon: The Assurance of Pardon is the Scripture-based pronouncement of God’s forgiveness following the corporate prayer of confession in Reformed worship.
summaries.assurance-salvation: Assurance of salvation is the settled, Spirit-wrought confidence that one is truly a child of God. It is not the same as salvation itself —
summaries.assurance: In Scripture, assurance is the God-given, Spirit-wrought confidence that one truly belongs to Christ and possesses eternal life.
summaries.astrology: A specific form of divination — reading the positions of celestial bodies as influences on human character or future events. Scripture's category for it is observing times (Heb.
summaries.atheism: Scripture does not argue for God's existence — it declares it. "The fool has said in his heart, 'There is no God'" (Psalm 14:1).
summaries.athens: The cultural capital of ancient Greece, philosophical center of the Mediterranean world, and the site of Paul's most famous engagement with intellectual culture.
summaries.atonement-blood: Atonement blood is the blood of sacrificial animals — and supremely of Christ — by which atonement is made for sin.
summaries.atonement-day: The Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) was the holiest day of Israel's liturgical calendar —
summaries.atonement-theories: The atonement is the work of Christ on the cross by which He reconciles sinners to God.
summaries.atonement: Atonement is the satisfaction of God's holy wrath against sin through the substitutionary death of Christ, resulting in reconciliation between God and man.
summaries.attributes-of-god: The Attributes of God are the qualities or perfections of God's being —
summaries.audacity: Audacity is holy boldness — the willingness to dare great things for God when the moment calls for it. David had audacity when he ran at Goliath with five smooth stones.
summaries.augustine-figure: Augustine of Hippo (354-430) was the bishop, theologian, and former rhetorician whose Confessions and City of God shaped Western Christianity for fifteen centuries.
summaries.augustinianism: The theological tradition flowing from Augustine of Hippo (354-430 AD), characterized by distinctive doctrines of grace, sin, and predestination.
summaries.authenticity: Scripture never commands believers to "be authentic" in the modern sense of expressing whatever they feel. It commands them to be truthful, sincere, and without hypocrisy.
summaries.author-intent: Author Intent is the hermeneutical principle that the meaning of a text is determined by what the author intended to communicate, not by what readers wish or feel.
summaries.authoritarianism: Scripture teaches that all authority derives from God: "There is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God" (Romans 13:1).
summaries.authority-biblical: All authority flows from God. Christ declared, "All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth" (Matthew 28:18).
summaries.authority: Authority is the God-given right to exercise power within a defined sphere, for the benefit of those under it.
summaries.autonomy: Scripture affirms human agency and responsibility — God made man a choosing being, not a puppet.

summaries.avi-ad: Avi-Ad (אֲבִי־עַד) — "Everlasting Father" — is the messianic title in Isaiah 9:6: "For unto us a child is born...
summaries.avocado-toast: Cultural shorthand for the Millennial generation's spending habits as critiqued by Boomers.
summaries.avodah: Avodah (עֲבוֹדָה) is the Hebrew word that fuses work, service, and worship into one concept.
summaries.awakening: Spiritual awakening is the sovereign work of God in reviving His people from spiritual slumber and bringing the lost to saving faith.
summaries.awe: Awe in Scripture is the soul's natural and proper response to encountering the living God —
summaries.baal-worship: Baal Worship is the Canaanite religion centered on Baal (storm-god) and Asherah (his consort).
summaries.baal: Baal (Hebrew "lord, owner") was the chief Canaanite storm-fertility god, perpetual rival of YHWH for Israel’s allegiance throughout the period of the judges and kings.
summaries.babel-tower: The Tower of Babel was the post-flood monument built on the plain of Shinar (Genesis 11:1-9) by humanity united in language and rebellion: "let us build us a city and a tower,…
summaries.babel: The city built by rebellious humanity in the plain of Shinar (Genesis 11:1–9), whose tower was designed to reach heaven and make a name for its builders —
summaries.babylon-city: Babylon is the Bible's city of man in confrontation with the city of God.
summaries.babylon-revelation: The symbolic name in Revelation for the worldly economic-religious system arrayed against the Lamb.
summaries.babylon: Babylon is the Bible's great anti-city -- the counterfeit of Jerusalem, the embodiment of human rebellion organized into civilization.
summaries.babylonian-exile: The seventy-year deportation of the southern kingdom of Judah to Babylon following the destruction of Solomon's temple in 586 BC;
summaries.back-biblical: "You will see my back, but my face shall not be seen" (Ex 33:23) — Moses was allowed to see only God's back.
summaries.backslider: A backslider is one who turns away from God after having professed allegiance to Him. Scripture uses the language of turning, wandering, and departing.
summaries.backsliding: The spiritual condition of one who has known God's ways and gradually turned away — not through a single dramatic defection, but through a slow, imperceptible drift of the heart.
summaries.bahnsen: Greg Bahnsen (1948-1995) was the American Reformed theologian who became the most effective popularizer of Cornelius Van Til's presuppositional apologetics.
summaries.balaam-figure: Mesopotamian diviner from Pethor on the Euphrates, hired by Balak king of Moab to curse advancing Israel (Num 22-24). Knew enough of YHWH to fear Him;
summaries.balaam: Balaam was the Mesopotamian seer hired by Balak king of Moab to curse Israel as they approached the Promised Land. God overruled him: he could only bless what God had blessed.
summaries.balak: Balak was the king of Moab who, terrified of Israel's approach as they marched from Sinai toward Canaan, hired Balaam the seer to curse them (Num 22-24).
summaries.balm: In Scripture, balm is both a literal aromatic healing resin and a powerful symbol of divine comfort, restoration, and the sufficiency of God's healing presence.
summaries.banner: The banner is the biblical image of visible identity and divine rescue. Every tribe of Israel camped under its own degel in the wilderness (Num 2:2), marking order and loyalty.
summaries.baptism-believer: Believer’s baptism is the public immersion of a repentant confessor in water in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
summaries.baptism-doctrine: Baptism is the ordinance by which Christ's people are publicly identified with Him. It is the visible sign of the new covenant, parallel to circumcision in the old.
summaries.baptism-jesus: The baptism of Jesus inaugurates His public ministry and is one of the clearest Trinitarian moments in all of Scripture.
summaries.baptism-modes: Baptism modes are the three principal Christian forms in which water has been applied: immersion (going under), pouring (affusion, water poured over), and sprinkling (aspersion).
summaries.baptism: A sacred ordinance instituted by Jesus Christ in which a believer is immersed in (or washed with) water as an outward sign of inward spiritual reality —
summaries.baptismal-regeneration: The question of baptismal regeneration centers on whether water baptism causes or merely signifies regeneration.

summaries.barabbas: Barabbas is one of the most remarkable details in the Passion narrative. His name — Bar Abba — literally means "son of the father." Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John all mention him.
summaries.barak: Barak son of Abinoam was the military commander summoned by Deborah the prophetess to lead Israel against Sisera and the army of Jabin king of Canaan (Judges 4-5).
summaries.barbarism: Scripture recognizes the reality of barbarism — the descent of human civilization into cruelty, lawlessness, and savagery that results from rejecting God.
summaries.barley: Barley is the Bible's grain of the humble and the resurrection. Because it ripened first — a wave-sheaf of barley was offered on the day after Passover Sabbath (Lev 23:10-11) —
summaries.barn: A barn is the storage building for harvested grain.
summaries.barnabas: Barnabas was a Levite from Cyprus who sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet (Acts 4:37) —
summaries.barren-fig-tree: Christ's parable in Luke 13:6-9. A man planted a fig tree in his vineyard. For three years he came seeking fruit and found none.
summaries.barrenness: Barrenness in Scripture is a condition that God alone can remedy. Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel, Hannah, and Elizabeth were all barren —
summaries.bartholomew: Bartholomew was one of the Twelve, named in all four apostle lists (Mt 10, Mk 3, Lk 6, Acts 1) but never given a separate biographical scene in the Synoptics or Acts.
summaries.bartimaeus: Bartimaeus was the blind beggar by the road outside Jericho who, hearing Jesus pass, cried out Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me. The crowd tried to silence him;
summaries.bashan: Bashan was the fertile, well-watered tableland east of the Sea of Galilee, famous in Scripture for its strong cattle (Psalm 22:12; Amos 4:1) and great oaks (Isaiah 2:13).
summaries.basileia: Basileia is the sovereign reign and rule of God over all creation — not a geographic territory but the dynamic exercise of divine kingship.
summaries.batach: Batach (בָּטַח) is the Hebrew verb for trust — different from aman (to be firm, the root of amen and emunah).
summaries.bathsheba: Wife of Uriah the Hittite; taken by David in adultery while Uriah was at war (2 Sam 11); first child died as judgment on the sin (2 Sam 12);

summaries.be-strong: The divine command to take courageous strength, given as preparation for the conquest in Joshua 1 ("be strong and of a good courage" appears three times in 1:6, 7, 9).
summaries.beam-eye: Christ's figure in Matthew 7:3-5 of the timber-beam (Greek dokos —

summaries.beard: The hair of the male chin and lower face; in Scripture, the visible mark of manhood, age, and dignity, and an ornament Levitical law explicitly protected.
summaries.beast-mode: Sports-and-gym slang for a state of maximum performance intensity: total focus, total effort, total commitment. From Marshawn Lynch's nickname (NFL, c. 2009).
summaries.beast-of-revelation: The two beasts of Revelation 13 together form the satanic counterfeit of Christ and His church. The first beast rises from the sea —
summaries.beast: In Revelation 13 and 17, the eschatological figures who arise to oppose the Lamb.
summaries.beatific-vision: The Beatific Vision is the direct, unmediated sight of God enjoyed by the redeemed in the new creation.
summaries.beating-breast: Beating the breast is the gesture of striking one’s own chest as a public sign of grief, unworthiness, or repentance. Luke uses it twice with weight.
summaries.beatitude-1: The first of Christ's beatitudes (Matt 5:3): Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
summaries.beatitude-2: The second of Christ's beatitudes (Matt 5:4): Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted. The Greek pentheo denotes deep grief, especially over loss or sin.
summaries.beatitude-3: The third Beatitude of Christ’s Sermon on the Mount is "Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth" (Matthew 5:5) — drawing directly on Psalm 37:11.
summaries.beatitude-4: The fourth of Christ's beatitudes (Matt 5:6): Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
summaries.beatitude-5: The fifth of Christ's beatitudes (Matt 5:7): Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy. Mercy here is active — the merciful do mercy, show mercy, give mercy —
summaries.beatitude-6: The sixth of Christ's beatitudes (Matt 5:8): Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God. Purity here is internal — en te kardia, in the heart.
summaries.beatitude-7: The seventh Beatitude is "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God" (Matthew 5:9).
summaries.beatitude-8: The eighth and longest of Christ's beatitudes (Matt 5:10-12): Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
summaries.beatitude: A beatitude is a declaration of blessedness — a pronouncement by God that a person or condition is in a state of divine favor and flourishing.
summaries.beatitudes: The eight blessings opening Christ's Sermon on the Mount (Matt 5:3-12; cf. Luke 6:20-26).
summaries.beauty-biblical: Biblical beauty begins with God. David's one desire was "to gaze upon the beauty of the LORD" (Psalm 27:4).
summaries.beauty: The created harmony, fittingness, and glory that reflects the character of God. Beauty is one of the three classical transcendentals — truth, goodness, beauty —
summaries.beelzebub: Originally the Philistine god of Ekron consulted by Ahaziah king of Israel (2 Kgs 1:2-6);
summaries.beelzebul-baal: Beelzebul (Beelzebub) is the New Testament title for Satan deriving from the Old Testament Philistine deity Baal-Zebub of Ekron (2 Kgs 1:2-6).
summaries.beersheba: The southernmost major city of biblical Israel, in the Negev desert.
summaries.begotten: In its most crucial theological usage, "begotten" describes the eternal relationship between God the Father and God the Son —
summaries.behaviorism: Scripture teaches that human beings are not stimulus-response machines but moral agents with an inner life that matters profoundly to God.
summaries.behemoth: The great creature YHWH points to in Job 40:15-24, paired with leviathan in chapter 41 in YHWH's whirlwind-speech to Job. "Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee...

summaries.beholding: The sustained, intentional contemplation of God's glory — the spiritual discipline of turning the eyes of faith toward Christ and holding that gaze.
summaries.being: God reveals Himself as the ground of all being: "I AM WHO I AM" (Exodus 3:14). The divine name YHWH declares that God is self-existent —

summaries.beloved: In Scripture, "Beloved" is first and foremost a title for Jesus Christ —
summaries.belt-of-truth: The belt of truth is the first piece of the armor of God: stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth.
summaries.belt-truth: The first piece of the whole armor of God in Ephesians 6:14: having your loins girt about with truth. The Roman soldier's belt was the foundational garment —

summaries.benediction-formula: The pronounced blessing closing a worship service.
summaries.benediction: A benediction is the authoritative pronouncement of God’s favor and peace upon His covenant people. It is not a wish, a hope, or a polite farewell —
summaries.benedictus: The Benedictus is the prophecy of Zechariah at the birth of John the Baptist (Luke 1:68-79).
summaries.benevolence: The active disposition to seek the good of others, rooted in the character of God who is good and does good (Ps. 119:68).

summaries.berakhah: A berakhah is the Jewish formal blessing-prayer structured as Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who....
summaries.berea: Berea was a Macedonian city about fifty miles southwest of Thessalonica where Paul and Silas preached after fleeing the riot at Thessalonica (Acts 17:10-15).
summaries.bereavement: Scripture does not minimize grief. Jesus wept at the tomb of Lazarus (John 11:35), even though He was about to raise him from the dead.
summaries.bernice: Bernice was the eldest daughter of Herod Agrippa I, sister to Agrippa II and Drusilla.
summaries.bestiality: Sexual acts between humans and animals. Scripture's prohibition is direct, comprehensive, and capital: Leviticus 18:23 forbids it for both sexes;
summaries.bestie: "Bestie" is the casual diminutive of best friend, often performative — used freely on social media for relationships of widely varying depth.
summaries.bethany: The Judean village two miles from Jerusalem on the eastern slope of the Mount of Olives; home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus — the friends Christ loved —
summaries.bethel: Bethel — Hebrew "house of God" — was the town between Ai and Luz where Jacob saw the ladder reaching to heaven, with the angels of God ascending and descending.
summaries.bethlehem: Bethlehem is a small town in the hill country of Judah, about five miles south of Jerusalem, whose significance in redemptive history far exceeds its size.
summaries.betray: To deliver a person into the hands of an enemy through deception, breaking covenant trust.

summaries.betrothal: In Scripture, betrothal is a binding covenant commitment to marriage, not a mere engagement or expression of intent.
summaries.bezalel: Bezalel is the first person in Scripture of whom it is said that God "filled him with the Spirit of God" (Exodus 31:3).

summaries.bible-translation: Bible Translation is the work of rendering the Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek Scriptures into other languages so each tongue may read God's words.

summaries.bigotry: The word "bigotry" does not appear in Scripture, but the concept it originally described — irrational hatred of persons based on their identity rather than their actions —
summaries.binah: Binah (בִּינָה) is the Hebrew word for understanding — specifically the insight that distinguishes, separates, and weighs.
summaries.binary: The Bible is built on binary distinctions established by God Himself. Light and darkness. Heaven and earth. Land and sea. Male and female. Good and evil. Life and death.
summaries.bind-strong-man: Bind the strong man is Christ's phrase in Matthew 12:29: or else how can one enter into a strong man's house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he…

summaries.binding-loosing: Binding and loosing is the rabbinic vocabulary Christ uses in Matthew 16:19 and 18:18 to describe the authority given first to Peter and then to the church: whatsoever ye shall…
summaries.bingeable: Streaming-era Millennial adjective for content engineered to be consumed in long uninterrupted sessions: cliffhanger structure, addictive plot devices, auto-play timing.

summaries.curse: A divinely authorized pronouncement of separation, judgment, and forfeit — the opposite of blessing.

summaries.cyrene: Cyrene was a major North African city (in modern Libya) with a substantial Jewish population —

summaries.damascus: Damascus is one of the oldest cities in the world — still inhabited from before the time of Abraham until today.

summaries.dan-tribe: Dan was the fifth son of Jacob — born to Bilhah, Rachel’s maid — and the tribe descended from him (Genesis 30:6).
summaries.dancing-before-lord: Dancing before the LORD is the embodied, public, sometimes uninhibited expression of joy at His salvation.
summaries.daniel-book: The fourth of the Major Prophets, twelve chapters covering the seventy-year ministry of Daniel in the courts of Babylon and Persia (605-535 BC).

summaries.daniel: Daniel is the prophet of the exile and the revealer of God's sovereign plan over all earthly kingdoms.

summaries.dark-night-of-the-soul: Scripture records many instances of believers experiencing spiritual desolation — seasons where God's presence feels withdrawn and the soul is overwhelmed with grief.
summaries.darkness-biblical: Darkness in Scripture begins as a condition over the formless deep before God says "let there be light" (Gen 1:2-3).
summaries.darkness: Darkness in Scripture is first physical — the formless void before God spoke light into existence (Genesis 1:2-3).

summaries.davidic-covenant: The Davidic Covenant is God's unilateral promise to David that his throne would endure forever.

summaries.day-laborer: A day laborer is a worker hired for the day — paid at sundown, expected to feed his family on what he earned that day.

summaries.day-of-lord-nt: The Day of the Lord in the New Testament is the eschatological day of Christ’s return in glory, bringing final judgment on the wicked and final salvation to the church.
summaries.day-of-the-lord: The Day of the LORD is the prophetic day of the LORD's decisive intervention in history for judgment of His enemies and salvation of His people.
summaries.day-of-yhwh: The Day of YHWH (Old Testament Yom YHWH) is the eschatological day of God’s decisive intervention, bringing both judgment of the wicked and salvation of the faithful.
summaries.day: The basic biblical unit of time, reckoned in Hebrew thought from evening to evening (and the evening and the morning were the first day, Gen 1:5);
summaries.dayspring: Dayspring is one of Scripture's most evocative names for the Messiah. In the Benedictus — Zechariah's prophetic song at the birth of John the Baptist —
summaries.deacon: A deacon is a recognized servant-leader in the local church, appointed to care for the practical needs of the congregation —

summaries.dead-works: Dead works are religious activities performed without faith, apart from the life-giving power of God.
summaries.death-penalty: The death penalty is instituted by God in the Noahic covenant: "Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed, for God made man in his own image" (Genesis 9:6).
summaries.death-to-self: Death to self is the daily crucifixion of one's own will, desires, and ambitions in submission to Christ.
summaries.death: Scripture presents death as fundamentally separation — three kinds: (1) Physical death: the separation of soul from body (Gen. 3:19);
summaries.debauchery: Debauchery (aselgeia) in Scripture describes the open, shameless indulgence of the flesh — a life given over to sensual excess without restraint or remorse.
summaries.deborah: Deborah (Hebrew Devorah, "bee") was a prophetess and judge of Israel during the period of the judges — one of the most remarkable women in Scripture.
summaries.debt-biblical: Scripture treats debt on two levels. Financially, debt places a man under bondage to his creditor: "The borrower is the slave of the lender" (Proverbs 22:7).
summaries.deceit: Deceit is the deliberate misrepresentation of reality with the intent to mislead.
summaries.deception: Deception is the active misrepresentation of truth in order to mislead, manipulate, or control. In Scripture, deception is Satan's primary weapon —
summaries.decline-narrative: Scripture presents history not as a story of inevitable human progress but as a drama of creation, fall, redemption, and consummation under God's sovereign hand.
summaries.decolonize: The Great Commission is, by definition, a colonizing mandate — not of land, but of hearts.
summaries.deconstruction-faith: Deconstruction (in the religious sense) is the process by which many raised in Christian homes systematically take apart the faith they were taught and evaluate each piece against…
summaries.deconstruction: Scripture has a word for what modern culture calls "deconstruction" — it is apostasy. "They went out from us, but they were not of us;
summaries.decree: A divine decree is God's eternal, sovereign, and irrevocable determination of all that shall come to pass.
summaries.dedication: The setting apart of a person, place, or thing for sacred use; the formal handing-over to the Lord's service.
summaries.deep-state: Scripture is clear that earthly powers are not what they appear.
summaries.defamation: To defame someone is to bear false witness — a direct violation of the ninth commandment (Exodus 20:16).
summaries.definitive-sanctification: Definitive sanctification is the decisive, one-time break with sin’s dominion that takes place at conversion —
summaries.deification: Deification — or theōsis — is the biblical doctrine that redeemed humanity is called to participate in the divine nature through union with Christ.
summaries.deism: The God of Scripture is not an absentee landlord. He is intimately involved in every detail of His creation. "In him we live and move and have our being" (Acts 17:28).
summaries.deity-of-christ: The Deity of Christ is the doctrine that Jesus is fully God — one essence with the Father, eternally begotten, sharing all divine attributes. The Word was God (Jn 1:1);

summaries.delight: The intense, joyful pleasure of the soul in what it loves and values most.
summaries.deliver-from-evil: The seventh and final petition of the Lord's Prayer: "deliver us from evil" — or, more precisely (the Greek has the article), "deliver us from THE evil one.
summaries.deliver: The act of God rescuing His people from bondage, danger, sin, or enemies — one of the most dominant themes in all of Scripture. Deliverance is not merely help;
summaries.deliverance: Deliverance is God's decisive, sovereign act of rescuing His people from bondage, danger, or oppression — by His power alone, not human effort.
summaries.deluge: The worldwide flood of Genesis 6-9 by which God judged the violent and corrupt antediluvian world, sparing only Noah, his three sons, their wives, and the animals on the ark.
summaries.demas: Demas is one of the saddest character arcs in the New Testament — appearing in just three Pauline texts.
summaries.demetrius: Demetrius was an Ephesian silversmith who made silver shrines of the goddess Diana (Artemis) and saw his entire industry threatened by Paul's preaching.
summaries.demon: Demons are fallen spiritual beings — angels who rebelled with Satan and were cast out of heaven (Luke 10:18; 2 Pet. 2:4; Jude 6).
summaries.demonology: Scripture teaches that demons are fallen angels who rebelled with Satan (Revelation 12:7-9).
summaries.demure: Originally an English adjective for modesty, reserve, and quietness — virtues Scripture commends in 1 Tim 2:9 and 1 Pet 3:3-4.
summaries.denial-peter: On the night of Christ's arrest, Peter followed at a distance and entered the courtyard of the high priest. Three times in succession he was identified as a follower of Jesus;
summaries.denial: Peter's denial of Christ is the paradigm of sinful denial — refusing to confess what one knows to be true out of fear (Matthew 26:69-75).
summaries.denominationalism: Scripture commands unity among believers while insisting on doctrinal fidelity. Paul rebuked the Corinthians for saying "I follow Paul" or "I follow Apollos" —
summaries.deny-self: The first half of Christ's discipleship triplet in Matthew 16:24 (and parallels): If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
summaries.deny: To deny is to refuse, repudiate, or disown. Scripture sets two opposite movements side by side.

summaries.derbe: Derbe was a city in Lycaonia, the eastern frontier of Paul's first missionary journey. After being stoned at Lystra Paul came to Derbe and made many disciples there (Acts 14:20-21).

summaries.derision: Mocking laughter — the contemptuous response of the wicked toward the godly, and conversely, the LORD's response toward those who plot against His Christ.
summaries.desacralization: Scripture teaches that all of creation is sacred — declared "very good" by God (Genesis 1:31) and sustained by His word (Colossians 1:17).

summaries.desert: The desert (Hebrew midbar, Greek erēmos) is the uninhabited or barely-inhabited dry land — and Scripture loads it with theological freight.
summaries.desiderium: The deep, aching longing of the soul for God — an unsatisfied hunger that no earthly thing can fill because it was designed for an eternal object.
summaries.desire: An inward longing or craving directed toward an object — the engine of the human will. Desire itself is morally neutral, designed by God as the motivating force of the soul.
summaries.desolation: Desolation in Scripture is the devastating consequence of covenant unfaithfulness — a land or people stripped of God's blessing and presence, left emptied and ruined.
summaries.despair: Despair is the opposite of biblical hope. To despair is to declare that God cannot or will not act.
summaries.destiny: Scripture replaces vague cosmic "destiny" with the personal, purposeful plan of a sovereign God.
summaries.destruction-temple: The two historical destructions of the Jerusalem temple: (1) Solomon's temple by Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon in 586 BC, prophesied by Jeremiah, ending the Davidic monarchy;
summaries.detachment: Scripture teaches that attachment to the world is incompatible with love for God. "No one can serve two masters" (Matthew 6:24).
summaries.determinism: Scripture holds two truths in tension that determinism collapses into one: God is sovereign over all things, AND human beings are genuinely responsible moral agents.
summaries.deuteronomy: The fifth book of the Bible. Deuteronomy is Moses's farewell address to the second-generation Israelites poised to enter Canaan after their parents died in the wilderness.
summaries.devil: The Devil (also called Satan, the Adversary, the Accuser, the Serpent, and Beelzebul) is a specific created being —
summaries.devotion: The total consecration of the whole person — mind, will, affections, and practice — to God.
summaries.devout: A devout person is one who has organized their entire life around reverence for God. Devoutness is not occasional religious observance —
summaries.diaconia: Diaconia is the New Testament's master word for ministry and service in all its forms —

summaries.dichotomy: The dichotomist view holds that humans are body and soul/spirit.

summaries.dignity: Biblical dignity is the inherent worth, honor, and significance every human being possesses by virtue of being made in the image of God.

summaries.diligence: Diligence is the sustained, careful application of effort to one's work, calling, and spiritual life.
summaries.disagree: To hold a different judgment than another. Not in itself sinful —
summaries.discerning-spirits: Discerning of spirits (diakriseis pneumatōn) is the spiritual gift listed by Paul in 1 Corinthians 12:10 for distinguishing true from false spiritual influence in the assembly.
summaries.discernment-spirits: "Do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits to see whether they are from God" (1 John 4:1).
summaries.discernment: The God-given capacity to distinguish between truth and falsehood, good and evil, the Holy Spirit and counterfeit spirits.
summaries.disciple-making: Disciple-making is the central mandate of the church: "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them...
summaries.disciple: A disciple of Jesus Christ is not merely a student of information but an apprentice of a life. In ancient culture, disciples did not just attend lectures —
summaries.discipleship-cost: Jesus was explicit: "Let him deny himself and take up his cross daily" (Luke 9:23).
summaries.discipleship-deep: Intentional discipleship is the deliberate process of forming a Christian into Christ-likeness.
summaries.discipleship: Discipleship is the process of becoming like Jesus — in character, in mission, in relationship with the Father. Jesus did not invite people to a class; He said "Follow me" —
summaries.discipline-biblical: Biblical discipline runs in two forms — divine and ecclesial — and both are acts of love, not cruelty.
summaries.discipline: Discipline in Scripture is the loving, intentional work of training, correcting, and forming a person — child or believer — toward wisdom, godliness, and maturity.

summaries.dispensationalism: Dispensationalism is a system of biblical interpretation that divides redemptive history into distinct eras (dispensations) —

summaries.diversity: Scripture affirms that God created a world of magnificent variety — nations, tongues, peoples, and gifts — all under the unified lordship of Christ.

summaries.divided-monarchy: The period after Solomon's death when the kingdom split: ten northern tribes under Jeroboam (the kingdom of Israel, 931-722 BC, ending with Assyrian conquest);

summaries.divine-impassibility: Divine impassibility is the classical Christian doctrine that God in His divine nature is not subject to passions imposed from outside Himself.
summaries.divine-simplicity: Divine simplicity teaches that God is not composed of parts — His being, attributes, and will are identical with Himself.

summaries.doctrine: The body of authoritative teaching delivered by Christ and the apostles; the content of revealed truth that forms, guards, and transmits the Christian faith.

summaries.domestic-church: The Christian household is the foundational unit of discipleship.

summaries.doomscrolling: The habit of compulsively scrolling through negative content — news, social media, comment threads, world events —
summaries.door-sheep: Christ's self-designation in John 10:7-9: I am the door of the sheep... by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved.

summaries.doorkeeper: A doorkeeper is the appointed gatekeeper of a household, palace, or sanctuary — the one who decides who crosses the threshold and who does not.
summaries.doorpost: The doorpost is the vertical beam on either side of a doorway — and Scripture loads it with three theologically charged uses.

summaries.dorcas: A disciple of Joppa, also called Tabitha, “full of good works and almsdeeds”; she fell sick and died;
summaries.double-mindedness: Double-mindedness is the spiritual condition of divided loyalty — wanting the benefits of following God while refusing to surrender the pleasures of the world.
summaries.double-portion: The double portion is, in Old Testament inheritance law, the firstborn's share — twice that of any other son (Deut 21:17).
summaries.double-predestination: Double predestination is the biblical teaching that God's eternal decree encompasses both the salvation of the elect and the condemnation of the reprobate.

summaries.dove: The dove is Scripture's gentle sign and the Spirit's chosen emblem. The dove Noah released returned with the olive leaf, signaling new creation after the flood (Gen 8:11).
summaries.dowry: The dowry — properly, the bride-price in biblical custom — was the payment a man made to the bride’s father in order to marry her.

summaries.dragon: In Scripture, the dragon is the symbolic embodiment of Satan and the chaos powers arrayed against God.
summaries.dread: In Scripture, dread carries both a negative sense — the terror that comes upon God's enemies — and a positive sense —
summaries.dream-biblical: God frequently used dreams for revelation.
summaries.dream-vision: Dream visions are God's ordinary mode of prophetic communication, named in Numbers 12:6: If there be a prophet among you, I the LORD will make myself known unto him in a vision,…
summaries.drink-offering: The drink offering (nesek) was a libation of wine poured out before the LORD as an accompaniment to the daily burnt offerings, Sabbath offerings, and festival sacrifices.
summaries.drunkenness: The sin of habitual or excessive intoxication; named explicitly in the works-of-the-flesh lists (Gal 5:21, Rom 13:13) and disqualifying for elders (1 Tim 3:3, Titus 1:7).
summaries.drusilla: Drusilla was the Jewish daughter of Herod Agrippa I (the king who killed James the brother of John, Acts 12:1-2), and the third wife of the Roman procurator Felix —

summaries.dualism-gnostic: Gnostic dualism teaches that matter is evil and spirit is good —
summaries.dulia: The Greek douleia in Scripture refers to service or bondage -- never to a graded system of religious veneration.
summaries.dunamis: The inherent, operative power of God — not merely His capacity to act but His actual energy in motion.
summaries.dust-returns: The biblical statement of human mortality with the body's return to its created material. Genesis 3:19 announces it as the curse of the fall ("unto dust shalt thou return");
summaries.dust: Dust is the fine earth from which man was formed and to which his body returns — Scripture’s emblem of human frailty, mortality, and absolute dependence on the Creator.
summaries.duty-biblical: Duty in Scripture is what one owes by virtue of position and relation. Solomon at Ecclesiastes' close: fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
summaries.duty: Solomon concluded: "Fear God and keep his commandments, for this is the whole duty of man" (Ecclesiastes 12:13).
summaries.dwell-biblical: To dwell is to settle permanently, not merely to visit.
summaries.dwell: To dwell in Scripture is not merely to occupy space — it carries the weight of settled, covenantal presence.
summaries.dwelling: The theme of God dwelling with His people is the central thread of the entire biblical narrative. The garden of Eden was a dwelling place of God with man.
summaries.dynamite: Boomer-era superlative meaning excellent, awesome, top-tier. Peaked in the 1970s; permanently associated with the catchphrase from Good Times.
summaries.dystopia: "Dystopia" — the modern literary term for a deliberately bad social order — has long been forecast by Scripture.
summaries.eagle: The eagle in Scripture is the emblem of divine mothering-strength, renewal, and swift judgment.
summaries.ear-biblical: Hearing in Scripture is almost always prior to seeing. God called; Israel was to hear ("Hear, O Israel," Deut 6:4).
summaries.ear-discipline: The discipline of guarding what the ear receives.
summaries.ear: The organ of hearing; in Scripture, the body part associated with the chief duty of the believer — to hear the voice of God.

summaries.early-rising: Early rising is the discipline of rising before the world’s noise to seek God in the day’s first quiet —
summaries.earnest: In its theological sense, earnest is a pledge or down payment guaranteeing a future full inheritance.
summaries.earnestness: Earnestness is wholehearted, unhurried intensity directed toward what is truly important. It is the opposite of halfheartedness, casualness, or going through the motions.
summaries.earthen-vessels: "We have this treasure in jars of clay, to show that the surpassing power belongs to God and not to us" (2 Corinthians 4:7). The treasure is the gospel;
summaries.east-of-eden: East of Eden is Genesis 3:24's phrase for the place of Adam and Eve's exile after the fall: so he drove out the man;
summaries.easter: Easter celebrates the central event of the Christian faith: Christ's bodily resurrection (1 Corinthians 15:3-4).
summaries.easy-peasy: Mid-20th-century children's reduplicative phrase for very easy; Boomer-era mainstream. The slang is purely expressive.

summaries.moderation: Scripture does commend a form of moderation — but it is not what the modern world means by the word. Paul writes, "Let your moderation be known unto all men.
summaries.modesty-biblical: Biblical modesty is the discipline of measure in apparel, speech, and self-presentation — the refusal to display what is properly hidden or to seek attention by display.
summaries.modesty-clothing: The holy restraint that clothes the body to honor God and neighbor.
summaries.modesty: Modesty is the virtue of appropriate restraint — in dress, speech, ambition, and self-presentation.
summaries.molech: The Ammonite and Canaanite deity associated with child sacrifice — passing the seed through the fire.

summaries.money-biblical: Scripture treats money as a stewardship entrusted by God, to be used for His purposes and according to His principles.
summaries.money: Money is the medium of exchange — morally neutral as a tool, but deeply tested in the heart’s love, use, and worship of it.
summaries.monism: The most fundamental distinction in all of reality, according to Scripture, is the Creator-creature distinction. God is self-existent, eternal, and infinite;

summaries.mood: One-word slang for identification with a feeling state — usually a relatable, mild misery (tired, overwhelmed, lazy).
summaries.moral-courage: Moral courage in Scripture is the willingness to obey God and speak His truth at the cost of comfort, reputation, or life itself.
summaries.moral-influence: The Moral Influence theory (associated with Peter Abelard, 12th c., and many liberal theologians since) teaches that Christ’s death moves us morally —
summaries.moral-law: The moral law is the eternal, unchanging expression of God's holy character revealed to man as the standard of righteousness.
summaries.moral-relativism: Scripture demolishes moral relativism at its foundation. God's moral law is absolute because it flows from His unchanging character. "I the LORD do not change" (Malachi 3:6).
summaries.moralistic-therapeutic-deism: Moralistic Therapeutic Deism (MTD) is the unspoken religion of modern American Christianity — the actual belief system underneath the official one.

summaries.moriah: Mount Moriah is the mountain where Abraham offered Isaac (Gen 22) and where Solomon later built the temple (2 Chron 3:1).

summaries.morning: Morning in Scripture is the time of new mercies, divine visitation, and resurrection. "Weeping may tarry for the night, but joy comes with the morning" (Ps 30:5).
summaries.mortification: Mortification is the ongoing, Spirit-enabled work of killing sin in the believer's life — not managing it, not negotiating with it, but actively putting it to death.
summaries.moses: Moses is the great lawgiver, prophet, and deliverer of Israel —
summaries.mother: A woman who bears, nurses, nurtures, and raises children — a sacred vocation that Scripture honors as foundational to civilization.
summaries.motherhood-biblical: Biblical motherhood is the state and office of being a mother — with its dignity, formative power, and recognized weight. Eve was named the mother of all living (Gen 3:20);

summaries.mount-olivet: The Mount of Olives is a ridge east of Jerusalem, separated from the temple mount by the Kidron Valley. It is one of the most significant locations in the life of Christ.
summaries.mount-sinai: Mount Sinai is the specific mountain where God descended in fire and smoke to give the law to Moses and establish His covenant with Israel.
summaries.mount-tabor: A prominent isolated mountain rising about 1,900 feet above the Jezreel Valley in lower Galilee.
summaries.mount-transfiguration: The Mount of Transfiguration is the unnamed mountain where Jesus was visibly transformed before Peter, James, and John.
summaries.mount-zion: Mount Zion began as the specific hill David conquered from the Jebusites, becoming the City of David (2 Samuel 5:7).
summaries.mountain-motif: The Mountain Motif is the recurring biblical setting of theophany, covenant-making, and decisive encounter with God.
summaries.mourn-comforted: "Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted" is the second Beatitude of Christ’s Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5:4).
summaries.mourning: Mourning, in Scripture, is public, sustained, often communal lamentation over death, sin, exile, or covenant betrayal —
summaries.mouth-biblical: "Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks" (Matt 12:34). Scripture treats the mouth as a heart-meter. Confession is made with the mouth (Rom 10:9-10);
summaries.mouth: The bodily aperture for speech, eating, and breath; in Scripture, the chief outlet of the heart's contents.
summaries.multiculturalism: The political-cultural ideology that the coexistence of multiple distinct cultures within a single polity is a positive good and proper public goal —
summaries.multiply: To multiply is to increase greatly — and Scripture loads the verb with covenant freight.
summaries.multitude-counsellors: The "multitude of counsellors" is the wisdom-principle of decision-making by submitted counsel from multiple wise voices —

summaries.murder: The unlawful killing of a human being made in the image of God; the sixth commandment of the Decalogue (Ex 20:13).
summaries.murmuring: Murmuring is the low, persistent complaint of the heart given voice — a grumbling discontent against God’s providence and His ordained servants.
summaries.mustard-seed-faith: "If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, 'Move from here to there,' and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you" (Matt 17:20).
summaries.mustard-seed: Christ's parable of the kingdom of heaven (Matt 13:31-32; Mark 4:30-32;
summaries.mustard: A common garden plant of Palestine grown from a tiny round seed;
summaries.muster-biblical: To muster is to call together, count, and inspect — the formal showing of troops.

summaries.myrtle: A fragrant evergreen shrub native to Israel;

summaries.narrative: Scripture is itself a narrative — but not merely a human one.

summaries.nehemiah: Nehemiah was a Jewish exile who rose to cupbearer of Artaxerxes I of Persia — a position of high trust.
summaries.neighbor: The fellow human placed within reach of one's life and care; in the Levitical and Christian ethic, the proper object of love after God Himself.

summaries.nepsis: Nepsis is the practice of spiritual watchfulness —

summaries.new-earth: The renewed earth of the consummated kingdom;

summaries.nifty: Mid-twentieth-century mild positive adjective for something cleverly designed or attractively practical. Era-stamped: that's a nifty trick, nifty little gadget.
summaries.night-watch: A night watch is the guard kept through the dark hours when the household sleeps.
summaries.night: The hours of darkness from sunset to dawn;

summaries.nineveh-city: The capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire, on the eastern bank of the Tigris River opposite modern Mosul, Iraq. Nineveh was one of the largest cities of the ancient world —
summaries.nineveh: Nineveh was the capital of the Assyrian empire, the most feared and brutal military power of the ancient Near East.
summaries.no-condemnation: Paul's verdict opening Romans 8: "There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit.

summaries.noah: Noah was the tenth generation from Adam, a righteous man who "walked with God" in an age of universal corruption (Genesis 6:9).
summaries.nobility: In the biblical worldview, true nobility is not inherited status but a quality of character —

summaries.nothingness: Nothingness is the state of non-being — what would obtain if God had not spoken creation into existence.
summaries.nous: In Paul, nous (νοῦς) is the faculty of rational and moral perception — the human mind as oriented either toward God or away from Him.
summaries.npc: "NPC" — a gaming term for "non-player character," the scripted background figures populating a video game —

summaries.nurture-admonition: Nurture and admonition is the KJV pair in Ephesians 6:4: bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

summaries.obey: To obey is to listen under — to submit to authority.

summaries.ohio: Gen Alpha / Gen-Z slang use of the state name Ohio as a generic descriptor for the weird, chaotic, or absurd. A meme-coded vocabulary marker.

summaries.revelation-book: Revelation (Greek Apokalypsis, "unveiling") is the capstone of Scripture — John’s apocalyptic vision given on Patmos around AD 95.
summaries.revelation: Revelation is God's initiative to make Himself known. Since God is infinite and man is finite, finite man cannot discover infinite God on his own — God must reveal Himself.
summaries.reverence-biblical: Biblical reverence is the settled inner posture of awe before God, His Name, His house, His Word, His messengers, and His ordained authorities.
summaries.reverence: Reverence is the outward expression and inner posture of awe, honor, and holy fear before God and, derivatively, before those He has placed in positions of dignity.
summaries.reviler: One who speaks abusively, attacks character, and dishonors with the tongue.
summaries.reviling-wife: A wife whose speech to and about her husband is habitually contemptuous, mocking, defaming, undermining, or publicly shaming. Scripture does not soften the category.
summaries.revival: Revival is the sovereign work of God's Spirit powerfully renewing the life of the church —
summaries.revivalism: True revival is a sovereign work of God in which He pours out His Spirit upon His people, producing deep conviction of sin, genuine repentance, renewed faith, and transformed lives.
summaries.reward-heaven: The eschatological recompense laid up for the faithful.
summaries.rhema: Rhema is the specific, spoken, living word of God — Scripture proclaimed, declared, and applied by the Spirit with divine power.
summaries.rhoda: A young servant girl (Greek paidiske) in the house of Mary the mother of John Mark, where the church was praying for Peter's release.
summaries.rich-fool: The Parable of the Rich Fool begins with an interruption. A man in the crowd called out, "Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance with me" (Luke 12:13).
summaries.rich-man-lazarus: Christ's account in Luke 16:19-31. A rich man clothed in purple and fine linen feasted sumptuously every day; Lazarus, a beggar full of sores, lay at his gate desiring crumbs.
summaries.rich-young-ruler: A wealthy young ruler approached Christ asking what good thing shall I do, that I may have eternal life? Christ pointed to the commandments; the man claimed to have kept them all.
summaries.ridicule: Mockery employing humor to belittle; the device of Sanballat against Nehemiah's wall, of Israel's enemies against the prophets, and of the world against Christ's people (Neh 4:1-3;
summaries.right-hand-of-god: The Right Hand of God is the position of supreme honor and active power. Psalm 110:1 prophesies the Messiah's session there;
summaries.righteous-anger: Holy indignation against sin and injustice. Paul commands: be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath (Eph 4:26, quoting Ps 4:4).
summaries.righteous-branch: Jeremiah's specific Messianic title: "I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth" (Jer 23:5;
summaries.righteousness: Righteousness is conformity to God's character and law — being and doing what is right as defined by the Creator. It has two dimensions in Scripture: (1) Forensic righteousness —
summaries.rights: In the biblical framework, humans bear genuine dignity and certain just claims because they are image-bearers of God (Genesis 1:26–27).
summaries.rise-biblical: To rise in Scripture climbs a theological ladder: rising from sleep, rising from prayer, rising to go, rising from death.
summaries.river-life: The river of the water of life proceeding from the throne of God and the Lamb in the New Jerusalem.
summaries.river-of-life: The River of Life is Revelation 22:1's phrase for the river of water of life proceeding from God's throne and the Lamb's in the new Jerusalem.
summaries.river: The river, in Scripture, is a recurring mark of God’s presence and provision. Eden had four rivers flowing out from the garden —
summaries.rizzler: One who has rizz — charismatic romantic-attraction skill. The slang celebrates a particular kind of social capacity: the ability to charm, flirt, attract.
summaries.robe: A long, full-length outer garment of honor; in Scripture, the priest's blue robe with bells and pomegranates (Ex 28);
summaries.rock-ages: Christ as the eternal, unshakable foundation. The image is sounded throughout Scripture: the LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer (Ps 18:2; cf. 2 Sam 22:2, Deut 32:4);
summaries.rock: The Rock in Scripture is God Himself — solid, immovable, elevated, shelter in storm, source of water in the desert, foundation of faith.
summaries.rod-and-staff: The rod and staff are the shepherd’s two tools in Psalm 23:4: "thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
summaries.rod-of-correction: The rod of correction is the biblical instrument and figure for the loving discipline of children.
summaries.rod-of-jesse: Isaiah 11:1's Messianic image: "And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots.
summaries.rod-staff: The shepherd's twin instruments in Psalm 23:4: thy rod and thy staff they comfort me.
summaries.rod: The rod is the Bible's tool of authority, discipline, defense, and rule. A shepherd's rod fights off predators and disciplines straying sheep (Ps 23:4);
summaries.romans-book: Paul's longest letter, written from Corinth around AD 57 to a church he had not yet visited. Romans is the most theologically systematic letter in the New Testament.
summaries.rome: Rome was the capital of the most powerful empire in history and the political backdrop against which the entire New Testament unfolds.
summaries.root-david: A Messianic title used twice in Revelation: the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed (Rev 5:5);
summaries.root-of-david: Christ's self-title in Revelation 5:5 ("the Root of David, hath prevailed") and 22:16 ("I am the root and the offspring of David").
summaries.rose: The rose, in Scripture, is a wild meadow-bloom of the plain of Sharon.
summaries.royal-priesthood: The biblical identity of all believers as priests to God under Christ the great High Priest.
summaries.ruach: Ruach is the Hebrew word at the center of biblical cosmology, anthropology, and pneumatology.
summaries.rule-of-faith: The rule of faith is the body of essential Christian doctrine delivered by the apostles and received by the church as the authoritative summary of the gospel.
summaries.rule-of-life: An intentional, written rhythm of practices — prayer, Word, work, rest, fellowship, service — ordered to keep the disciple aligned with Christ over the long haul.
summaries.rule: To rule, in the biblical sense, is to exercise delegated authority within a God-ordained sphere —
summaries.ruler: A ruler is one appointed to exercise governing authority over a people, a household, or a domain — not by his own initiative but by God's sovereign placement.
summaries.run-biblical: The Bible walks more than it runs, but it runs at critical moments. The father of the prodigal ran to meet his returning son (Luke 15:20) —
summaries.ruth-book: Ruth is the short, luminous narrative of covenant loyalty (chesed) set in the days of the judges.
summaries.ruth-covenant: Ruth's covenant is the verbal covenant Ruth makes with Naomi at Bethlehem's road: whither thou goest, I will go;
summaries.ruth-figure: Ruth was a Moabite woman who married Mahlon (son of Naomi); was widowed; refused to leave her bereaved mother-in-law (thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God);
summaries.ruth: Ruth is a Moabite widow who chose to follow Naomi back to Bethlehem, uttering one of the greatest declarations of covenant faithfulness in Scripture: "Your people shall be my…
summaries.ryle-jc: J. C. Ryle (1816-1900) was the English evangelical Anglican who served as first Bishop of Liverpool (1880-1900).
summaries.sabbatarianism: The Sabbath principle is established at creation: "God rested on the seventh day from all his work" (Genesis 2:2-3).
summaries.sabbath-keeping: The discipline of weekly ceasing from labor to rest in God's finished work —
summaries.sabbath-rest: The seventh-day rest commanded at creation (Gen 2:2-3), codified in the fourth commandment (Ex 20:8-11), fulfilled and reframed in Christ (Heb 4:9-11).
summaries.sabbath-work-rest: The Sabbath is the seventh-day rest God established at creation (Genesis 2:2-3) —
summaries.sabbath: The seventh day set apart by God at creation as a day of rest and holy convocation — rooted not in the Mosaic law but in the very pattern of creation itself (Gen 2:2–3).
summaries.sacerdotal: Of or relating to the priesthood — particularly the Levitical priesthood of the Old Covenant and its fulfillment in Christ as the Great High Priest.
summaries.sackcloth-ashes: Sackcloth and ashes is Scripture’s combined sign of profound grief or repentance. Sackcloth (Hebrew saq) was a coarse, dark, scratchy garment of goat-hair worn next to the skin —
summaries.sackcloth: Sackcloth is the biblical outward sign of an inward crisis — worn for grief, for repentance, for humbling before God, and for prophetic warning.
summaries.sacrament: A sacrament (or ordinance in Baptist/Reformed usage) is a visible, outward rite that signifies, seals, and (in some traditions) conveys an inward spiritual grace, instituted by…
summaries.sacramentalism: Scripture commands two ordinances: baptism and the Lord's Supper.
summaries.sacred-assembly: The set-apart gathering of God's people called by divine command. Hebrew miqra qodesh (holy convocation) —
summaries.sacred-secular-divide: Scripture knows no sacred-secular divide. "The earth is the LORD's and the fullness thereof" (Psalm 24:1).
summaries.sacred: The sacred is that which has been set apart by God or for God — separated from the common and consecrated to holy purposes.
summaries.sacrifice-system: The sacrifice system established in Leviticus was God's ordained means for dealing with sin under the Old Covenant.
summaries.sacrifice: The offering of something of value — particularly life — to God, either as worship, as expiation for sin, or as dedication of oneself.
summaries.sacrilege: Sacrilege is the violation of the boundary between the holy and the common — the invasion of the sacred by the profane.
summaries.sacrosanct: That which is so holy, so set apart by God's own decree, that to violate it is to invite divine judgment. The sacrosanct is not merely important or valued —

summaries.sadducees: The Sadducees were the wealthy priestly aristocracy of Jesus' day. They traced their name and lineage to Zadok, the high priest under David and Solomon.

summaries.saint: A saint is anyone who has been set apart (sanctified) by God through faith in Jesus Christ.
summaries.sainthood: In the New Testament, every believer is a saint. Paul addresses his letters "to the saints" at Corinth, Ephesus, Philippi, and Colossae —
summaries.salome-dancer: Salome was the daughter of Herodias by her first husband Philip.
summaries.salome: In the Gospels, the disciple Salome is present at the crucifixion (Mark 15:40) and at the empty tomb (Mark 16:1).
summaries.salt-and-light: "You are the salt of the earth;
summaries.salt-covenant: A salt covenant is an unbreakable agreement marked by the shared eating of salt — the symbol of preservation, purity, and indissoluble bond.
summaries.salt-earth: Christ's designation for His disciples in the Sermon on the Mount: ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is…
summaries.salt-of-earth: Christ's image in Matthew 5:13: "Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be…
summaries.salt: Salt in the Bible preserves, covenants, and flavors. Every sacrifice was to be seasoned with salt: "with all your offerings you shall offer salt" (Lev 2:13).
summaries.salus-extra-ecclesiam: Scripture teaches that salvation is in Christ alone —
summaries.salutation-pastoral: The Pastoral Salutation is the minister’s pronouncement of grace and peace at the start of worship in the name of the triune God —
summaries.salvation: Salvation is the comprehensive rescue of humanity from sin, its guilt, its power, and its eternal consequences —
summaries.samaria: Samaria served as the capital of the northern kingdom of Israel after the division under Rehoboam.
summaries.samaritan-woman: The Samaritan Woman at the Well is the unnamed woman of John 4 to whom Christ revealed Himself as the Messiah. She had had five husbands; the man she was with was not her husband.
summaries.samaritan: The mixed-religion population of central Israel descended from intermarriage between exiled Northern Israelites and Assyrian colonists (2 Kings 17);
summaries.samaritans: The Samaritans were the remnant of the northern kingdom of Israel after the Assyrian conquest (722 BC), mixed with foreign peoples resettled there by Assyria (2 Kings 17:24-41).
summaries.samson-figure: Samson was the last and most tragic of Israel’s judges (c. 1075 BC) —
summaries.samson: Samson is the last of the great judges, a Nazirite from birth, set apart by God to begin the deliverance of Israel from the Philistines (Judges 13:5).
summaries.samuel-prophet: Samuel was the son of Hannah’s prayer-promise — born after long barrenness, given back to the LORD, and raised in the tabernacle at Shiloh under Eli the priest (1 Samuel 1-3).
summaries.samuel: Samuel was the transitional figure between the judges and the monarchy.
summaries.sanctification-progressive: The lifelong process by which the justified believer is gradually conformed to the image of Christ.
summaries.sanctification: Sanctification is the ongoing work of God's Spirit in the believer, progressively conforming them to the image of Christ. It follows justification and continues until glorification.

summaries.sanctity-of-life: The sanctity of human life is grounded in the imago Dei — the image of God imprinted on every human being at conception.
summaries.sanctity: Sanctity is the quality of holiness — the condition of being set apart to God and therefore inviolable.
summaries.sanctuary: A sanctuary is a holy place — a space set apart for the presence of God, separated from the common and profane, where God dwells with His people and they draw near to Him.
summaries.sanctus: The Sanctus (Latin "holy") is the threefold "Holy, Holy, Holy" sung by the seraphim around the throne in Isaiah’s vision: "And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy,…
summaries.sandals-peace: The fifth piece of the whole armor of God: your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace (Eph 6:15).
summaries.sanhedrin: The Sanhedrin was the highest Jewish court, composed of 71 members including the high priest, chief priests, elders, and scribes.
summaries.sarah: Sarah is the wife of Abraham, the mother of Isaac, and the matriarch of the covenant people.

summaries.satan: The personal name of the chief adversary of God and His people; introduced in Job 1-2 as the Satan (the accuser before the heavenly council);

summaries.saul-king: Israel's first king (~1050-1010 BC), anointed by Samuel at YHWH's reluctant concession to Israel's demand for a king "like the nations." Tall, handsome, initially humble;
summaries.saul: First king of Israel; tall, handsome, modest at his anointing, but rapidly proud and disobedient on the throne.
summaries.save-life: The shadow side of Christ's discipleship paradox in Matthew 16:25 (and parallels): whosoever will save his life shall lose it;
summaries.save: To save, biblically, is to rescue, deliver, preserve —
summaries.saving-grace: The grace of God in Christ that actually delivers sinners from condemnation and brings them to glory — not mere divine favor but redemptive power (Eph 2:5-8; Titus 2:11).
summaries.scapegoat-azazel: The scapegoat was the second goat of the Day of Atonement ritual in Leviticus 16.
summaries.scapegoat: On the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16), the high priest selected two goats by lot: one was sacrificed as a sin offering, its blood sprinkled on the mercy seat to satisfy divine…
summaries.scarlet: Scarlet in Scripture is the color of sin, sacrifice, and the costly. Rahab hung a scarlet cord from her window (Josh 2) — the sign that saved her household at Jericho.
summaries.scepter: The scepter is the biblical image of kingship and rightful rule. Jacob prophesied that "the scepter shall not depart from Judah" (Gen 49:10) —

summaries.schism: Schism is a sinful division within the body of Christ —
summaries.scientism: Scripture celebrates the study of God's creation -- "It is the glory of God to conceal things, but the glory of kings is to search things out" (Proverbs 25:2).

summaries.scoffer: A person whose habitual posture toward truth, authority, and divine warning is contemptuous mockery. Hebrew lets (scoffer, scorner).
summaries.scorn: Scorn is the disposition of contemptuous derision — the heart that mocks what God has spoken.
summaries.scorner: Scripture's Proverbs-vocabulary for the man whose disposition toward correction is contempt rather than receptivity. Hebrew lets (scorner, mocker, scoffer).

summaries.scribe: A scribe was a professional copyist, interpreter, and teacher of the Law of Moses.
summaries.scripture-memory: Scripture memory is the discipline of internalizing the Word of God verse-by-verse —

summaries.scroll-sealed: The seven-sealed scroll of Revelation 5 that only the Lamb is worthy to open.
summaries.scroll: In the ancient world, a scroll was the primary medium of written revelation — a roll of papyrus or animal skin containing sacred text.
summaries.sea-motif: The Sea Motif is the recurring biblical figure of chaos, judgment, and threat to God's ordered creation. The Spirit hovers over the waters at creation, separating them;

summaries.sealing: Sealing is the act of impressing a signet upon a document, deed, or person to authenticate and secure it.
summaries.seals-of-revelation: The seven seals of the scroll, opened by the Lamb in Revelation 5-8. The scroll is sealed with seven seals (Rev 5:1); the search for one worthy to open it fails (5:2-4);
summaries.second-adam: Second Adam (or Last Adam) is Paul's term in 1 Corinthians 15:45-49 and Romans 5:12-21 for Christ as the head of redeemed humanity. The first Adam was a living soul;
summaries.second-blessing: Scripture teaches that every believer receives the Holy Spirit at conversion — "Anyone who does not have the Spirit of Christ does not belong to him" (Romans 8:9).
summaries.second-coming-detail: The Second Coming is the bodily, visible, glorious return of Christ to judge the living and the dead and consummate His kingdom.
summaries.second-coming: The second coming of Christ is the certain, visible, bodily, glorious return of Jesus to judge the living and the dead, consummate His kingdom, and make all things new.
summaries.second-death: Eternal separation from God in the lake of fire. Revelation 20:14-15: And death and hell were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
summaries.secret-place: The "secret place" is the hidden, intimate refuge of YHWH’s presence — known by experience to the saint who dwells in it.
summaries.secularism: Secularism is not the same as neutrality — it is a worldview that claims neutrality.
summaries.seder: The ordered Passover meal commanded in Exodus 12 and retold annually by Jewish families across the Diaspora.
summaries.see-biblical: Seeing in Scripture ascends from eyeball to soul: physical sight, spiritual perception, prophetic vision, beatific vision. The prophets were called "seers" (1 Sam 9:9).
summaries.see: To see, biblically, goes beyond physical sight. The deeper meaning is perceptive recognition — seeing-with-understanding.
summaries.seed: The "seed" (zera) is the central thread of biblical redemption.
summaries.seek-his-face: "Seek His face" names the pursuit of God’s manifest presence rather than merely His benefits.
summaries.seeker-sensitive: Scripture does not describe the gathered worship of the church as an evangelistic event designed for unbelievers.
summaries.seer-biblical: A seer is the older Hebrew title for prophet, emphasizing the visionary dimension of the office: he that is now called a Prophet was beforetime called a Seer (1 Sam 9:9).

summaries.selah: A Hebrew term appearing 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3, traditionally understood as a liturgical or musical direction. The exact meaning is uncertain;
summaries.self-care: Self-care began as a useful clinical concept: patients managing chronic illness, veterans coping with trauma, caregivers preventing burnout.
summaries.self-control: Self-control (enkrateia) is the last of the nine fruits of the Spirit (Gal 5:22–23), and its position is significant — it is the governing virtue that directs all the others.
summaries.self-denial: The daily discipline of saying no to the demands of the autonomous self — appetites, ambitions, opinions — in order to say yes to Christ as Lord. The hinge of discipleship.
summaries.self-discipline: The ordering of one's own appetites, time, words, and habits under God's lordship. Greek egkrateia (self-mastery, temperance).
summaries.selfishness: Selfishness is the original sin. When Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit, they were placing their own desire above God's command —

summaries.seminary: Scripture does not prescribe a formal institutional model for pastoral training.
summaries.semper-fidelis: Semper Fidelis is Latin for “always faithful” — since 1883 the motto of the United States Marine Corps.

summaries.sensus-plenior: Sensus plenior is the deeper meaning of Scripture that the divine Author intended, which goes beyond (but does not contradict) what the human author consciously understood.

summaries.sentinel: A sentinel is a soldier on watch — the more formal cousin of the sentry.
summaries.sentry: A sentry is the soldier posted to perceive and report.

summaries.sergius-paulus: Sergius Paulus was the Roman proconsul of Cyprus during Paul's first missionary journey. A prudent man (Acts 13:7), he summoned Paul and Barnabas to hear the word of God.

summaries.sermon-on-mount: The Sermon on the Mount is the foundational ethical teaching of Christianity.
summaries.serpent-fiery: The saraph is the Bible's "burning" creature — serpentine in the wilderness, angelic in the throne room, bearing fire in both.

summaries.serpent-wise: The shrewd practical wisdom Christ commands of His disciples in mission.
summaries.serpent: The serpent is Scripture's chief image of Satan and the concentrated evil that tempted humanity into the fall.
summaries.servant-leadership: Servant leadership is the pattern of authority established by Christ Himself.

summaries.session-christ: The "session of Christ" is the technical doctrinal name for the seated reign of the risen, ascended Lord at the right hand of God.
summaries.seth-son: The third son of Adam and Eve, given as the replacement for Abel. Genesis 4:25-26: And Adam knew his wife again;

summaries.seven-deadly-sins: While Scripture does not enumerate a formal list of "seven deadly sins," it does identify root sins that produce all other transgressions.

summaries.seven-signs: The seven miraculous signs John's Gospel selects from Christ's ministry to unveil His identity.
summaries.seven-trumpets: The seven trumpets sounded by seven angels in Revelation 8-11, following the silence of the seventh seal.

summaries.shadow-almighty: The image of God's protective covering, especially in Psalm 91.
summaries.shadow-substance: Shadow and Substance is the Hebrews / Colossians distinction: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ (Col 2:17);
summaries.shadow-wings: The "shadow of His wings" is one of the most tender recurring images of YHWH’s protection in the Psalter —
summaries.shadow: The dim outline cast by light obstruction; in Scripture, used in two main senses. (1) Protection: the shadow of His wings, the shadow of the Almighty — sheltering nearness to God.

summaries.shadrach: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego were Daniel's three Hebrew companions in Babylonian captivity, given Babylonian names by their captors.
