summaries.shalom: Shalom is the comprehensive Hebrew concept of well-being that results when everything is as it should be — when creation, humanity, community, and God are in right relationship.
summaries.shame-godly: The painful awareness of having failed God or neighbor that drives toward repentance and life — distinguished from worldly shame which drives to despair (2 Cor 7:9-10; Ezek 16:63).
summaries.shame-toxic: Toxic shame is the condemning, identity-destroying false shame that says "I am wrong" rather than "I did wrong" —
summaries.shame: Biblically, shame functions on two levels. First, there is legitimate shame — the God-given moral signal that accompanies sin and exposure of guilt.
summaries.shechem: A central city in the hill country of Ephraim, situated in the pass between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. Abraham built his first Canaanite altar here (Gen 12:6-7);
summaries.sheep-and-goats: The Sheep and Goats is the climactic parable of Jesus' Olivet Discourse and one of the most sobering passages in the Gospels.
summaries.sheep-goats-parable: Christ's description of the final judgment in Matthew 25:31-46. The Son of Man comes in glory; all nations are gathered before Him; He separates the sheep from the goats.
summaries.sheep-goats: Christ's climactic Olivet parable in which the Son of Man, returning in glory, separates all nations as a shepherd divides sheep from goats —
summaries.sheep: Sheep function as one of Scripture's most pervasive and theologically loaded images. Sheep are simultaneously a picture of humanity's helplessness and God's faithful provision.
summaries.shekel-sanctuary: The shekel of the sanctuary was the standardized weight-of-silver used for tabernacle and temple offerings — set apart from the variable common shekel of the marketplace.
summaries.shekinah-glory: The visible manifestation of YHWH's dwelling-presence with His people: the cloud-and-fire pillar in the wilderness, the cloud filling the tabernacle (Exod 40:34-35) and Solomon's…
summaries.shekinah: The Shekinah is the visible, radiant manifestation of God's dwelling presence among His people.
summaries.shelter: Shelter is covered protection from storm, sun, or enemy.
summaries.shema: The great Jewish confession from Deuteronomy 6:4-9: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy…
summaries.shemittah-year: The shemittah (שְׁמִטָּה, "release") was the seventh-year Sabbath commanded for the land and for debt.
summaries.sheol: The Old Testament term for the realm of the dead;
summaries.shepherd-king: The biblical ideal of the king-as-shepherd of his people, rooted in David (the literal shepherd-boy made king) and developed in the prophets ("I will set up one shepherd over…
summaries.shepherd-leadership: Shepherd leadership is Christ’s pattern: feeding the flock, knowing the sheep by name, going before them, laying down His life for them.
summaries.shepherd-motif: The Shepherd Motif runs through Scripture as one of God's most pastoral self-portraits. Psalm 23 (the LORD is my shepherd);
summaries.shepherd: In Scripture, a shepherd is both a literal keeper of flocks and the supreme metaphor for God's relationship with His people. The LORD Himself is called "my shepherd" in Psalm 23.
summaries.shield-faith: The spiritual armor that extinguishes the enemy's attacks.
summaries.shield-of-faith: The shield of faith is the fourth piece of the armor of God: above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
summaries.shield: The shield is the Bible's image of God as the believer's active protector. "Fear not, Abram, I am your shield" (Gen 15:1) is the first divine self-designation of this kind.
summaries.shiloh: In its primary sense, the central sanctuary city of Israel from Joshua to Samuel, where the tabernacle stood and where Hannah prayed for Samuel (1 Sam 1).
summaries.shimei: Benjamite of Saul's house who cursed and threw stones at David as he fled Jerusalem during Absalom's rebellion (2 Sam 16:5-13).
summaries.shittim: The acacia wood of the Sinai wilderness; the only wood used in the construction of the tabernacle's sacred furnishings —
summaries.shoes-of-gospel: The shoes of the gospel are the third piece of the armor of God: and your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace.
summaries.shofar-trumpet: The ram's horn blown in Israel's assembly for war, worship, alarm, and feast. Hebrew shofar; Greek NT salpinx.
summaries.shofar: The shofar is Scripture's trumpet of covenant assembly, warning, and divine presence. God Himself descended on Sinai with the blast of an exceedingly loud shofar (Ex 19:16, 19;
summaries.shoulder: "The government shall be upon his shoulder" (Isa 9:6) — the Messianic title. The high priest carried the twelve tribes on his shoulders via the onyx stones on his ephod (Ex 28:12).
summaries.shout-for-joy: "Shout for joy" is the audible, loud, jubilant cry commanded as worship-response throughout the Psalms — not silent inner happiness but outward voiced jubilation.
summaries.showbread: The showbread was twelve loaves of unleavened bread arranged in two rows of six on a golden table in the Holy Place of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:30; Leviticus 24:5-9).
summaries.shrewd: Sharp-witted, prudent, practically wise in the navigation of complex situations.
summaries.side-biblical: "The rib that the LORD God had taken from the man he made into a woman" (Gen 2:22). The word tsela is "side" as much as "rib" — Eve came from Adam's side.
summaries.side-hustle: "Side hustle" is the current slang for secondary income work pursued alongside a primary job — freelance writing, app-driven driving, weekend consulting, online resale, etc.
summaries.sidon: The ancient Phoenician city on the Mediterranean coast north of Tyre, in modern Lebanon.
summaries.sign-covenant: A visible marker God has appointed as the public token of a specific covenant. Scripture names several.
summaries.sign-of-jonah: The Sign of Jonah is the only sign Christ promised to the unbelieving generation that demanded one: as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale's belly;
summaries.sign: A sign in Scripture is a visible, concrete reality that points beyond itself to God's character, covenant, or redemptive purpose. Signs are not ends in themselves — they signify.
summaries.signet: A personal seal-stone (often a ring) used by kings and nobles to authenticate documents, decrees, and ownership; pressed into wax or clay to leave an unforgeable mark.
summaries.silas: Silas (also called Silvanus) was a "leading man among the brethren" in Jerusalem (Acts 15:22) and a prophet (Acts 15:32).
summaries.silence-biblical: Silence in Scripture is not empty — it is reverent and attentive. "Be still, and know that I am God" (Ps 46:10). "The LORD is in his holy temple;
summaries.silence-discipline: Silence is the spiritual discipline of ceasing to speak and ceasing to be spoken to, so that God can be heard.
summaries.silence-god: The experience of God's apparent absence in the midst of suffering, prayer, or longing.
summaries.silence-of-god: The discipline of trusting and seeking God when heaven feels brass — the faith that endures through Habakkuk's “how long” and the Psalmist's “why”
summaries.silence: The disposition of restraint in speech and inward stillness before God;
summaries.silent-before-god: Silence before God is the settled hush Habakkuk commands the whole earth to keep when the LORD is in His holy temple: "But the LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep…
summaries.silent-years: The Silent Years are the roughly four centuries between Malachi's last words and Gabriel's announcement to Zechariah in the temple. No canonical prophet spoke during this stretch;
summaries.silver-biblical: Silver is Scripture's money metal and also its redemption metal. "Every one who is numbered... shall give half a shekel as an offering to the LORD...
summaries.simeon-niger: Simeon called Niger was one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch (Acts 13:1) — the first multi-ethnic congregation in Christian history.
summaries.simeon-temple: Simeon was an old man in Jerusalem who had been waiting his whole life for one moment.
summaries.simeon-the-just: Simeon was the aged just and devout man of Jerusalem (Lk 2:25-35) to whom the Holy Spirit had revealed he would not see death before seeing the Christ.
summaries.simon-magus: Simon Magus was a Samaritan sorcerer who astonished his city, professed faith under Philip's preaching, was baptized, but then offered Peter money to obtain the gift of laying on…
summaries.simon-of-cyrene: Simon of Cyrene was a passerby coming in from the country — almost certainly a North African Jew up for Passover —
summaries.simon-the-leper: Simon the Leper was a resident of Bethany at whose house Christ was anointed by Mary of Bethany shortly before the Passion (Mt 26:6-13, Mk 14:3-9).
summaries.simony: Simony is the commercialization of the sacred — the attempt to acquire spiritual power, office, or grace through money or worldly influence.
summaries.simple-one: The Proverbs category of the open-hearted but undiscerning person — not malicious, but easily led astray because lacking discernment. "The simple believeth every word" (Prov 14:15).
summaries.simple: In Proverbs, the simple (peti) is the person not yet wise and not yet committed to folly — teachable, persuadable, easily led for good or ill.
summaries.simplicity-divine: Divine Simplicity is the most metaphysically rigorous of the classical attributes. It holds that God is not composed of parts —
summaries.simplicity: The discipline of single-eyed devotion to God that frees the heart from divided loyalties.
summaries.simul-iustus-et-peccator: Simul iustus et peccator captures the paradox that Reformed and Lutheran theology affirms at the center of the Christian life.
summaries.simul-justus-et-peccator: Every believer exists in a permanent tension that cannot be resolved this side of glory: simul justus et peccator — simultaneously righteous and a sinner.
summaries.sin-offering: The sin offering (chattat) was prescribed for unintentional sins and ceremonial defilement. It addressed the pollution that sin brings to the worshiper and to the sanctuary.
summaries.sin-vs-iniquity: Scripture uses three different Hebrew nouns for moral wrong, each with its own shade — and modern English flattens all three to "sin," losing the precision.
summaries.sin: Sin is any want of conformity to, or transgression of, the law of God (1 John 3:4). It is fundamentally an offense against God's holy character —
summaries.sinai-experience: Israel's encounter with God at Mount Sinai (Ex 19-20) — the foundational event of the OT covenant.
summaries.sinai: Mount Sinai is the mountain of God's law-giving, the place where the LORD descended in fire, smoke, and thunder to establish His covenant with Israel.
summaries.sincerity-biblical: Purity of motive — unmixed, undisguised, free from the fillers of pretense. Greek eilikrineia (sincerity, purity) literally means tested by sunlight —
summaries.sincerity: Sincerity is freedom from pretense, deceit, and double-mindedness — the quality of being sun-tested, what holds up when the light falls full upon it.
summaries.sing: To produce musical sound with the voice in worship of God; commanded over fifty times in Scripture.
summaries.single-eye: The single eye is Jesus’ image in Matthew 6:22 for the heart whose loyalty is undivided: "The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall…
summaries.single-minded: "Single-minded" names the saint whose attention, allegiance, and aim are undivided.
summaries.sinner: In Scripture, "sinner" carries both a universal and a specific meaning.
summaries.sisera: Sisera was the Canaanite army-captain of Jabin king of Hazor — the great oppressor of Israel for twenty years (Judges 4:2-3).
summaries.sitz-im-leben: Understanding the historical setting in which a biblical text was written is a legitimate part of faithful interpretation. Paul wrote to specific churches facing specific problems.
summaries.six-day-work: Six-day work is the biblical labor pattern: six days of work followed by one of rest, week after week.
summaries.skandalon: A skandalon is a stumbling block — anything that trips a person into sin, unbelief, or spiritual ruin.
summaries.skepticism: Scripture commends discernment and testing of claims -- "Test everything; hold fast what is good" (1 Thessalonians 5:21).

summaries.sling: A simple shepherd's weapon of two cords and a leather pouch holding a smooth stone, swung overhead and released to fling the stone with high velocity;
summaries.sluggard: The sluggard is Proverbs' recurring antagonist: the chronically lazy man whose laziness has hardened into character.

summaries.snare-of-devil: The snare of the devil is Paul's metaphor for the devil's trap.
summaries.sneer: The silent or near-silent facial expression of contempt — mockery without words, dismissal with a curled lip.
summaries.sobriety: A quality of mind characterized by clear-headedness, self-restraint, and serious gravity —
summaries.social-construct: Scripture distinguishes between things God has established and things man has invented.
summaries.social-gospel: The biblical gospel is the good news that God saves sinners from the wrath to come through the death and resurrection of Jesus Christ.

summaries.sodomy: Homosexual sexual acts and certain other unnatural sexual practices.
summaries.soft-answer: The soft answer is the verse-encoded wisdom of Proverbs 15:1: "A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
summaries.soft-launch: "Soft launch" is the modern social-media practice of revealing a romantic relationship through indirect cues —
summaries.sojourn: To dwell temporarily in a land that is not one's own — to live as a resident alien, a stranger passing through, one who occupies space without claiming ownership.

summaries.sola-experientia: Scripture never elevates personal experience above the revealed Word of God.

summaries.sola-ratio: Scripture affirms that God gave humanity the capacity for rational thought — we are made in His image and called to love Him with all our mind (Matthew 22:37).

summaries.soldier-christ: Paul's charge to Timothy: Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ. No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life;
summaries.soldier: A man under military discipline and orders;

summaries.solitude-discipline: Solitude is the spiritual discipline of being alone with God.
summaries.solitude-extended: Extended solitude is the discipline of prolonged aloneness with God — hours, a day, a season —

summaries.solomon-figure: David and Bathsheba's son, third king of unified Israel (970-930 BC). The Lord appeared to Solomon at Gibeon and offered him whatever he asked;
summaries.solomon-wisdom: The God-given wisdom (chokmah) granted to Solomon at his accession (1 Kings 3:5-14) when he asked for an understanding heart to judge the people.
summaries.solomon: Solomon is the son of David and Bathsheba, the third king of Israel, the builder of the Temple, and the wisest man who ever lived apart from Christ.

summaries.son-of-david: A Messianic title rooted in the Davidic covenant (2 Sam 7:12-16), in which the Lord promised David an everlasting throne through his offspring.
summaries.son-of-god: The supreme New Testament title for Christ's eternal deity and unique relationship to the Father. He is not a son of God in the generic sense believers are sons by adoption;

summaries.sonship: The divinely granted status of being a son of God — received by adoption through faith in Jesus Christ (John 1:12; Gal. 3:26).

summaries.sorcery: Effectively a synonym for witchcraft, with particular emphasis on the use of drugs, potions, and ritual technique to access supernatural power apart from God.
summaries.sorrow: Grief and pain of heart arising from loss, sin, suffering, or separation from God —

summaries.soteriology: Soteriology is the systematic study of everything Scripture teaches about salvation: election, calling, regeneration, faith, repentance, justification, adoption, sanctification,…
summaries.soul-anchor: Christian hope as the anchor of the soul. Hebrews 6:19-20: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
summaries.soul-biblical: The Hebrew nephesh is broader than English "soul" — it names the whole living person animated by God's breath.
summaries.soul-competency: Soul competency teaches that every person stands before God as a responsible moral agent, directly accountable to Him, capable of receiving His revelation and responding in faith…

summaries.soul: The Hebrew nephesh is one of the most important and most misunderstood words in Scripture.

summaries.sovereignty: The sovereignty of God is His absolute, uncontested, underived authority and power over all things — angels, nations, nature, history, death, and every human heart.
summaries.sow-reap: The biblical law of cause-and-consequence in moral and spiritual life. Galatians 6:7-8: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.
summaries.sow: Scripture sows repeatedly: "Whatever one sows, that will he also reap" (Gal 6:7).
summaries.sower-explained: Christ's seed-and-soil parable in Matthew 13:1-23 is the only parable He explicitly interprets at length. The seed is the Word of the kingdom.
summaries.sower-parable: Christ's foundational parable about the kingdom of God's spread, found in all three synoptic gospels. A sower scatters seed;
summaries.sower: The Lord's opening parable in Matthew 13, Mark 4, and Luke 8: a sower casts the same seed (the Word) on four soils — the wayside, stony ground, thorny ground, and good ground —
summaries.sowing: The casting of seed onto plowed ground in expectation of a future harvest; in Scripture, the moral and spiritual counterpart of reaping.
summaries.sparrow: The sparrow is a small common bird sold cheaply in first-century markets — two sold for a farthing, five for two farthings (Matthew 10:29; Luke 12:6).
summaries.speak-biblical: God creates by speaking: "And God said, Let there be light" (Gen 1:3). The Word becomes flesh (John 1:14).
summaries.speak: To speak, in Scripture, is to utter words — but the word is freighted with creative and authoritative weight.
summaries.spear: The spear is the Bible's weapon of war and, finally, the instrument that pierced the Messiah. Goliath's spear had a shaft "like a weaver's beam" (1 Sam 17:7);
summaries.special-grace: The saving, regenerating, sanctifying grace given by God only to His elect —
summaries.special-revelation: Special revelation is God's specific, saving self-disclosure to humanity — through the prophets, through the written Scriptures, and supremely through His Son.
summaries.spectrum: God creates in categories, not spectrums. He made distinct kinds of animals, distinct kinds of plants, and He made mankind in two distinct sexes.
summaries.speech: Speech in Scripture is the use of words and is held to high accountability. Every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment (Mt 12:36).
summaries.sphere-sovereignty: Sphere Sovereignty is the doctrine that God has ordered human life into distinct spheres — family, church, civil government, education, commerce, arts —

summaries.spirit-human: Human spirit in Scripture is the God-breathed animating center of the person, closely related to but distinguishable from the soul.
summaries.spirit-truth: Christ's designation for the Holy Spirit in John 14-16, the title connecting the Spirit's specific work of guiding the apostolic church into all truth.
summaries.spirit: "Spirit" in Scripture refers primarily to: (1) the Spirit of God —
summaries.spiritual-abuse: Scripture warns repeatedly against leaders who exploit the flock.
summaries.spiritual-direction: The concept of spiritual guidance is deeply biblical. Moses counseled Joshua. Elijah mentored Elisha. Paul discipled Timothy.
summaries.spiritual-disciplines: Spiritual disciplines are the God-ordained means by which believers cooperate with the Holy Spirit in progressive sanctification.
summaries.spiritual-gifts-doctrine: Spiritual gifts are the endowments of the Holy Spirit given to every believer for the good of the church. Paul's word charismata is built on charis (grace) —
summaries.spiritual-gifts: Spiritual gifts are grace-endowments given by the Holy Spirit to each believer for the common good of the church.
summaries.spiritual-maturity: Spiritual maturity is the progressive growth of the believer toward the fullness of Christ.
summaries.spiritual-union: The Holy Spirit's work joining the believer to Christ — one aspect of the believer's union with Christ, with the Spirit emphasized as the bond.
summaries.spiritual-warfare-armor: Spiritual warfare is the believer’s daily combat —
summaries.spiritual-warfare-biblical: Spiritual warfare in Scripture is the real, ongoing conflict between God's people and the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.
summaries.spiritual-warfare: Spiritual warfare is the biblical framework for understanding the Christian life as a real conflict with real supernatural enemies.
summaries.spiritual-weapons: Spiritual weapons are the saint's arsenal in spiritual combat: not carnal but mighty through God for the pulling down of strongholds.
summaries.spreading-cloaks: Spreading the cloaks is the gesture by which a people received a king: they took their outer garments off and laid them on the road for him to ride or walk over.
summaries.spring-biblical: Spring is the Bible's resurrection season. Passover falls in spring (Nisan); barley is harvested; the firstfruits wave-sheaf is lifted;
summaries.spring-feasts: The four appointed feasts of the spring half of Israel's calendar (months 1-3, Nisan through Sivan): Passover (Pesach, Nisan 14), Unleavened Bread (Matzot, Nisan 15-21),…
summaries.springs-living-water: "Springs of living water" — or more precisely, "the fountain of living waters" —
summaries.sprinkled-blood: Sprinkled blood is one of Scripture’s great priestly motions —
summaries.sprinkling-baptism: Sprinkling is the mode of baptism in which water is applied by scattering drops upon the candidate.

summaries.staff: The staff is the biblical symbol of authority, pastoral care, and divine signature. Jacob crossed the Jordan with only his staff and came back two camps (Gen 32:10) —
summaries.stan: "Stan" — slang derived from Eminem’s 2000 song — names intense, often public devotion to a celebrity, product, fictional character, athlete, or idea.
summaries.standard-bearer: A standard-bearer is the soldier appointed to carry the unit's ensign — a position of conspicuous danger and conspicuous honor.
summaries.standing-firm: Paul's fivefold imperative in 1 Corinthians 16:13: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
summaries.steadfast: To be steadfast is to remain immovably fixed in loyalty, faith, or purpose — not by sheer willpower, but by being anchored to One who is immovable.
summaries.steadfastness: Steadfastness is the Spirit-wrought firmness of soul that does not waver under pressure, drift in seasons of ease, or quit under prolonged trial.
summaries.stephen-martyr: Stephen is the first Christian martyr — his name means "crown," which proved prophetic.
summaries.stephen: Stephen was one of the seven men chosen by the Jerusalem church to oversee the daily distribution to widows (Acts 6:5).

summaries.stewardship: Stewardship is the management of all that God has entrusted to a person — time, money, talents, body, relationships, creation —
summaries.stiff-necked: Stiff-necked is the biblical figure for stubbornly refusing instruction or correction, drawn from oxen that will not bend the neck to the yoke.
summaries.still-small-voice: The "still small voice" is the surprising mode of YHWH’s revelation to despondent Elijah on Mount Horeb in 1 Kings 19:11-13.

summaries.stilling-storm: Christ and His disciples were crossing the Sea of Galilee when a great storm arose. Christ slept in the stern.

summaries.stone-rejected: Psalm 118:22's prophetic image, applied to Christ by Christ Himself: The stone which the builders refused is become the head stone of the corner.
summaries.stone: Stone carries extraordinary theological density in Scripture. Stones mark covenantal moments — Jacob's pillow at Bethel becomes an altar stone (Gen 28:18);

summaries.stranger-pilgrim: The biblical identity of believers as temporary residents on earth.

summaries.transfiguration-event: The Transfiguration is one of the most stunning moments in the Gospels. Jesus took three disciples — Peter, James, and John —
summaries.transfiguration: The Transfiguration was the supernatural event on a high mountain where Jesus was transformed before His disciples —
summaries.transformationalism: Scripture teaches that Christ is Lord over all creation (Colossians 1:17-18) and that believers are to be salt and light in the world (Matthew 5:13-16).
summaries.transformed-mind: Paul commands believers not to be conformed to this world but to be transformed by the renewal of the mind, so that they may discern the will of God.
summaries.transgression: Transgression is willful, deliberate rebellion against a known law or covenant.
summaries.transvestism: The clinical / technical term for cross-dressing — the wearing of clothing of the opposite sex. Same biblical prohibition as cross-dressing (Deut 22:5: abomination, to'evah).
summaries.trash-adj: Dismissive adjective declaring something or someone worthless. The slang has two distinct uses: (1) of things (movies, products, services) — ordinary taste-judgment, harmless;
summaries.trauma: Scripture takes suffering with deadly seriousness. The Bible is not a book that minimizes pain —
summaries.travail: Travail is painful, exhausting labor or toil, often specifically the pain of childbirth.
summaries.treasure-earthen-vessels: Paul's image in 2 Corinthians 4:7 for the gospel-treasure carried in fragile human ministers: "But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may…
summaries.treasure-field: Christ's parable in Matthew 13:44 of a man who finds treasure hidden in a field, hides it again, and for joy thereof goes and sells all that he has to buy that field.
summaries.treasure-heaven: Jesus commands His disciples to store up treasures in heaven rather than on earth, where moth and rust destroy and thieves break in and steal.
summaries.treasure-store: Treasure store is the accumulated wealth or stored value — material or moral — that one has laid up.
summaries.tree-knowledge: The tree of the knowledge of good and evil was placed in the Garden of Eden alongside the tree of life.
summaries.tree-life: The tree of life stood in the center of the Garden of Eden, freely available to Adam and Eve.
summaries.tree-of-life: The Tree of Life stood in the midst of the garden of Eden (Gen 2:9). After the fall, access was guarded by cherubim with a flaming sword (Gen 3:24).
summaries.tree: The tree frames the entire biblical narrative —
summaries.trembling: "This is the one to whom I will look: he who is humble and contrite in spirit and trembles at my word" (Isa 66:2). "Work out your own salvation with fear and trembling;
summaries.trespass-offering: The Mosaic offering for specific sins involving violation of property, sacred things, or guilt requiring restitution. Hebrew asham (guilt offering, trespass offering).
summaries.trespass: A specific act of sin construed as a crossing of a boundary or a falling-aside from the path of obedience;
summaries.trial-faith: Scripture teaches that faith is tested and proven genuine through trials. Peter compares the testing of faith to gold refined by fire —
summaries.trials: Trials are God-permitted testings of the believer’s faith, intended to refine and prove what is genuine. They are not to be confused with sin’s own enticements —

summaries.tribalism: In Scripture, tribes are God-ordained divisions within a larger covenant people — a legitimate form of identity, inheritance, and organization under His rule.
summaries.tribulation: The pressure, affliction, and suffering appointed for believers in this age as they follow Christ in a hostile world.
summaries.trichotomy: The trichotomist view appeals primarily to Paul's prayer in 1 Thessalonians 5:23: "May your whole spirit and soul and body be kept blameless.
summaries.trigger-warning: Scripture does not shield people from hard truths — it delivers them. The prophets gave no trigger warnings before pronouncing judgment.
summaries.triggered: "Triggered" in modern usage names an involuntary distress response. Sometimes it is a real PTSD trigger — a sound, smell, or word that genuinely re-fires trauma neurology —
summaries.trinitarian: Trinitarian theology is the bedrock of Christian orthodoxy.

summaries.trinity: The Trinity is the Christian doctrine that the one God eternally exists as three distinct Persons — Father, Son, and Holy Spirit —
summaries.trisagion: The threefold declaration of God's absolute holiness — "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts" — spoken by angelic beings in the throne room of God.
summaries.triumphal-entry-event: Christ's deliberate entry into Jerusalem on the Sunday before His crucifixion (Palm Sunday), riding on a young donkey in fulfillment of Zechariah 9:9: thy King cometh unto thee...
summaries.triumphal-entry: Christ's deliberate, prophesied entry into Jerusalem on the first day of Passion Week, riding on a donkey's colt with the crowd spreading garments and palm branches and shouting…
summaries.triumphalism: Scripture teaches that Christ has definitively triumphed over sin, death, and the powers of darkness at the cross (Colossians 2:15).
summaries.trophimus: A Gentile believer from Ephesus who accompanied Paul on his return journey to Jerusalem (Acts 20:4) carrying the relief offering. His presence in the temple courts —
summaries.true-widow: "True widow" is Paul’s precise category in 1 Timothy 5:3-16: "Honour widows that are widows indeed.
summaries.trumpet-last: The last trumpet signals the return of Christ, the resurrection of the dead, and the transformation of living believers.
summaries.trumpet: The trumpet in Scripture is the instrument of divine announcement, alarm, assembly, and eschatological climax.
summaries.trumpets-feast: The first day of the seventh month, marked by the blowing of trumpets (shofar); a sabbath rest and holy convocation, opening the high holy days (Lev 23:23-25; Num 29:1-6).
summaries.trumpets-of-revelation: The seven trumpets of Revelation 8-11 are the second great cycle of judgments unsealed by the Lamb.
summaries.trust-lord: To trust in the Lord is the fundamental posture of biblical faith —
summaries.trust-radical: Radical trust is the faith that does not lean on its own understanding but commits its way wholly to the LORD. "Trust in the LORD with all thine heart;
summaries.trust: Trust, in the biblical sense, is an active, covenant-rooted reliance upon God's character and promises — not a passive sentiment but a posture of the will.
summaries.truth-sets-free: Jesus declared: "You will know the truth, and the truth will set you free" (John 8:32). In context, Jesus is not making a general statement about education or information.
summaries.truth: In Scripture, truth (emet in Hebrew; alētheia in Greek) is not merely factual accuracy — it is the very character of God. God is truth (Deut.
summaries.truthfulness: Truthfulness is the saint’s disposition of speaking and dealing in accordance with what is.
summaries.tsedaqah: Tsedaqah (צְדָקָה) is the Hebrew word for righteousness — but the concept is relational and covenantal rather than abstract moral perfection.
summaries.tsur: Tsur (צוּר) is the Hebrew word for rock — specifically the great cliff-face, the strong-rock, the immovable foundation.
summaries.tubal-cain: The pre-flood descendant of Cain remembered in Scripture as the first artificer of bronze and iron tools.
summaries.tubular: "Tubular" is the 1980s Gen-X surfer-coded superlative for excellent or awesome — a wave so perfectly curling that one rides through its tube.

summaries.turning-cheek: In Matthew 5:39, Jesus teaches: "If anyone slaps you on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.
summaries.turtledove: The turtledove is a small migratory dove whose annual return to the land of Israel marks the renewal of the year. "The flowers appear on the earth;
summaries.twelve-biblical: Twelve is the number of God's people. Twelve sons of Jacob become the twelve tribes of Israel. Jesus chose twelve apostles — a deliberate parallel meaning "new Israel.
summaries.twelve-tribes: The twelve sons of Jacob and their descendants, the foundational divisions of the covenant nation Israel.
summaries.twelve: In Scripture, the number of covenant government and ordered people. Jacob has twelve sons; Israel has twelve tribes; Christ chooses twelve apostles to govern the new Israel;
summaries.two-ages: The two ages are the biblical division of redemptive history into this age (Greek aiōn houtos —
summaries.two-debtors: Christ's parable to Simon the Pharisee in Luke 7:41-43, prompted by the sinful woman anointing His feet with tears, hair, and ointment.
summaries.two-kingdoms: The Two Kingdoms doctrine recognizes that God exercises His authority in two distinct ways.
summaries.two-masters: "No one can serve two masters." The statement is absolute. Jesus did not say it is difficult, or unwise, or risky. He said it is impossible.
summaries.two-sons-parable: Christ's parable in Matthew 21:28-32, told to the chief priests and elders. A man with two sons told the first to work in the vineyard;
summaries.two-trees: The Two Trees are the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil in the garden of Eden (Gen 2:9). One offers life on God's terms;
summaries.two-ways: The Two Ways is the wisdom-tradition image of two paths laid before every life: the way of righteousness leading to life, and the way of wickedness leading to destruction.
summaries.two-witnesses: The Two Witnesses are the two prophetic figures of Revelation 11:3-12. They prophesy clothed in sackcloth for 1,260 days;
summaries.tychicus: Tychicus was a beloved brother and faithful minister whom Paul sent on multiple critical errands across the Roman world.
summaries.type-antitype: Type and antitype is the technical hermeneutical pair: a type is an Old Testament person, event, or institution that prefigures a New Testament reality (the antitype).
summaries.type: A type, in biblical theology, is a divinely intended foreshadowing in Old Testament history of a New Testament reality — especially of Christ Himself.
summaries.typological-interpretation: Typology is the recognition that God has woven patterns of foreshadowing throughout redemptive history. Adam is a type of Christ (Romans 5:14).
summaries.typology: Typology is the recognition that God sovereignly ordered Old Testament history, persons, and institutions to serve as prophetic patterns (types) of New Testament realities…
summaries.tyre: The wealthy Phoenician city-state on the Mediterranean coast about 25 miles south of Sidon (in modern Lebanon).
summaries.tzedakah: Tzedakah is the Hebrew word for righteousness — but not as a private moral quality.
summaries.unbelief: The condition of not trusting God — whether through outright rejection or through practical failure to act on what one professes to believe.
summaries.unbeliever: An unbeliever is one who has not believed the gospel and remains in unbelief — Paul’s technical category for the unconverted.
summaries.unbridled: Unbridled describes a tongue, a passion, or a life with no governing strap — like a horse with no bit. James warns that a religion which fails to bridle the tongue is empty;
summaries.unchangeable: Unchangeable names the divine attribute by which God neither shifts in being, in will, nor in word.
summaries.unclean-spirit: The biblical category for demonic spirits, especially as encountered in the Gospels and Acts.
summaries.unclean: In Scripture, "unclean" operates on three levels: ritual, moral, and spiritual.
summaries.unconditional-election-doctrine: Unconditional Election is the doctrine that God's choice of whom to save was made in eternity past, not conditioned on anything He foresaw in the creature.
summaries.unconditional-election: Unconditional election teaches that before the foundation of the world, God chose certain individuals for salvation not because He foresaw that they would believe, but purely…
summaries.unction: Unction is the anointing of the Holy Spirit — the divine empowerment and consecration given to believers for knowledge, ministry, and service.
summaries.undefiled: Undefiled is the biblical word for what is pure, unstained, free from ceremonial or moral pollution.
summaries.under-the-sun: Ecclesiastes' framing for the human-eye-view of life: what is observable under the sun, considered apart from divine revelation. Used 29 times in Ecclesiastes.
summaries.undershepherd: The pastor or elder serving under Christ as Chief Shepherd, accountable to Him for the flock entrusted to his care.
summaries.understanding: Biblical understanding is the God-given capacity to discern truth, distinguish between good and evil, and perceive the meaning of God's revelation.
summaries.unequally-yoked: To be unequally yoked is to be harnessed to a partner whose nature, pace, and direction differ so much that the joint pull is destructive to both.
summaries.unfailing-love: The Hebrew hesed — God's covenant-faithful, loyal-loving steadfast love.
summaries.unfeigned: "Unfeigned" — KJV for without pretense, without play-acting, without a mask — names the inward reality matching the outward show.
summaries.unforgivable-sin: The blasphemy against the Holy Spirit named by Christ as the one sin that has no forgiveness.
summaries.unforgiving-servant: Christ's parable in Matthew 18:23-35, given as direct application of Peter's question about how often to forgive.
summaries.unhinged: "Unhinged" originated as a clinical description of mental instability — a door come loose from its frame.
summaries.union-with-christ-doctrine: Union with Christ is the theological framework that holds all of salvation together. Christians are not just forgiven; they are in Christ.
summaries.union-with-christ: Union with Christ is the foundational relational reality of salvation —
summaries.unity: Biblical unity is rooted in the eternal oneness of the Trinity — "the LORD our God, the LORD is one" (Deut 6:4) — and flows from that divine reality into the community of believers.
summaries.universalism: Universalism is the theological error that all people will ultimately be saved, either without faith in Christ or after purgatorial correction.
summaries.unleavened-bread: Unleavened bread commemorates the speed of redemption and the purity of the redeemed. Israel ate it leaving Egypt because the dough had no time to rise (Ex 12:34-39).
summaries.unsearchable: "Unsearchable" — KJV for what is past finding out — appears at the height of doxology in Scripture, not at the limit of frustration.
summaries.unspotted: Free from the world's stains; the second half of pure religion James names.
summaries.unstable: Wavering, unsteady, double-minded. James 1:6-8 names the disposition that gets nothing in prayer: For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord.
summaries.unteachable: The heart that refuses instruction. Proverbs returns to this theme repeatedly as a marker of the fool, the scoffer, and the stiff-necked.

summaries.upholding: Upholding is the continual sustaining of a thing in being — the holding-up of what would otherwise fall.
summaries.upper-room-discourse: John 13-17 records the longest connected teaching of Jesus in the Gospels, delivered to the eleven disciples on the night of His betrayal.
summaries.upper-room: The large furnished upper-story room where Christ ate the Last Supper with His disciples (Mark 14:13-16;
summaries.upright: A person of moral straightness — one whose life is aligned with God's standard of righteousness, who walks without crookedness, deception, or double-dealing.
summaries.ur-chaldees: The ancient city in southern Mesopotamia from which God called Abram out by faith.
summaries.urim-thummim: The mysterious objects placed in the high priest's breastplate of judgment, by which God communicated specific decisions to Israel before the era of established prophets.
summaries.urim: The urim (and its companion thummim) were sacred objects kept in the breastplate of judgment worn by the high priest (Exodus 28:30). Their exact form is unknown —
summaries.usury: Usury, in biblical usage, is the lending of money at interest to a brother in need — explicitly forbidden in the Mosaic law (Exodus 22:25; Leviticus 25:36-37; Deuteronomy 23:19-20).
summaries.utilitarianism: Scripture does not measure morality by majority happiness. God's law defines right and wrong regardless of utilitarian outcomes.
summaries.uttermost-parts: The uttermost parts are the farthest reaches — of the earth, of the sea, of the morning.
summaries.vacillation: Vacillation is the defining sin of the double-minded man. James is direct: "He who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
summaries.vagabond: A wanderer without settled home, in Scripture nearly always a negative category indicating either divine curse or unsettled spiritual disposition.
summaries.vainglory: Vainglory is the sinful craving for human praise and empty honor.
summaries.valiant: Valiant — KJV for "brave, courageous, mighty in battle" — is one of the great masculine words of Scripture. Saul gathered "any strong man, or any valiant man" (1 Samuel 14:52);
summaries.validation: Validation is the establishment that something is genuine. Modern usage often centers on emotional approval;
summaries.valley-shadow: The dark valley through which the believer walks under the LORD's shepherding.
summaries.valor-biblical: Biblical valor is strength-of-worth proven in real combat — the inner mettle that holds up under the test, displayed by warriors, prophets, and saints.
summaries.valor: Valor is courage in action — the strength of character that enables a person to do what is right and true in the face of danger, opposition, or loss.

summaries.vanity-of-vanities: "Vanity of vanities" is Ecclesiastes’ opening and closing refrain: "Vanity of vanities, saith the Preacher, vanity of vanities; all is vanity" (Ecclesiastes 1:2; 12:8).
summaries.vanity: "Vanity of vanities, all is vanity" — Qohelet's opening declaration (Eccl 1:2) does not express nihilism but profound theological realism. Hebel means vapor —

summaries.veil-temple: The temple veil was a thick curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn with cherubim woven into it (Exodus 26:31).

summaries.veracity: Veracity as a divine attribute means that God is essentially truthful in His being, His words, and His acts.

summaries.verity: A truth so foundational that it cannot be overturned by circumstance, culture, or consensus. In Scripture, verity is rooted not in human discovery but in divine self-disclosure.
summaries.vessel-honor: Paul's image in 2 Timothy 2:20-21: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.
summaries.vestigia-dei: Scripture asserts that God has not left himself without witness in creation. The heavens declare his glory (Ps 19:1); his invisible attributes — eternal power and divine nature —

summaries.vesture: Vesture is clothing — especially the outer garment, the public-facing layer of a person. Scripture loads the word with three theological uses.
summaries.vexation-biblical: Vexation is the shaking, grinding, or tormenting of the soul by trouble. Solomon uses it as a refrain in Ecclesiastes — vanity and vexation of spirit —
summaries.vexation: Vexation is severe distress of spirit, harassment, or agitation. It is the great refrain of Ecclesiastes: "all is vanity and vexation of spirit" (Ecclesiastes 1:14, 17; 2:11; 4:4) —
summaries.via-dolorosa: The Via Dolorosa is the path Jesus walked from Pilate's judgment hall to Golgotha, bearing His cross.
summaries.viator: The concept of viator captures the biblical truth that human life is essentially a pilgrimage — a journey from creation toward the final glory of God. We are not home yet.
summaries.vicar: Scripture identifies only one who acts as Christ's representative on earth: the Holy Spirit.
summaries.vicarious: Vicarious means acting or suffering in the place of another.
summaries.victim-mentality: Victim mentality is the settled habit of interpreting life through the lens of one's own victimization.
summaries.victory-christ: The triumph believers share in by union with the risen Christ. 1 Corinthians 15:57: thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
summaries.victory: Victory in Scripture is conquest over enemies, especially over sin, death, and the devil through Christ. This is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith (1 Jn 5:4).

summaries.vigilance: Vigilance is sustained, alert watchfulness against danger — the spiritual discipline of guarding the heart, the household, the church, and the doctrine entrusted to one’s care.

summaries.vindication: Vindication is the public, authoritative declaration by God that a person's cause is righteous —
summaries.vine-branches: Christ's defining metaphor for the believer's living dependence on Him.
summaries.vine-motif: The Vine Motif begins with Israel as God's vine (Ps 80, Isa 5, Jer 2, Hos 10) — carefully planted, watered, fenced, and yet bearing wild grapes.
summaries.vine-of-israel: The recurring prophetic image of Israel as the vine YHWH planted, tended, and grew —
summaries.vine-true: The seventh I-am saying of Christ in John's Gospel: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman (John 15:1).
summaries.vine: The vine is one of Scripture's richest covenantal images.
summaries.vinedresser: A vinedresser is the skilled tender of grapevines — specifically, the one who prunes, props, and prepares the vines for fruit-bearing.
summaries.vinegar: Soured wine, the cheap drink of Roman soldiers and laborers; in Scripture, offered twice to Christ on the cross —
summaries.vineyard-keeper: The vineyard keeper is the patient husbandman of grapes — pruner, watcher, harvester.
summaries.vineyard-theology: The Vineyard movement draws from George Eldon Ladd's "already/not yet" framework of the kingdom: Christ's kingdom has broken into history but awaits consummation.
summaries.vineyard: The vineyard is one of Scripture's richest symbols for the covenant relationship between God and His people.
summaries.viper-brood: Brood of vipers (KJV: generation of vipers) is the unsparing rebuke John the Baptist and Jesus addressed to the religious establishment whose teaching kept producing the same…
summaries.viper: The viper is a venomous serpent of the desert, often striking from concealment —
summaries.virgin-birth: The doctrine that Jesus Christ was conceived in the womb of Mary by the Holy Spirit without any human father.
summaries.virginity: Scripture honors virginity both as a practical gift for undivided devotion to the Lord and as a moral expectation before marriage.
summaries.virtue-signaling: Virtue signaling is public moral display whose primary purpose is to advertise the virtue of the signaler, not to accomplish anything good.
summaries.virtue: Biblical virtue is not merely moral rule-following but the formation of excellent character that naturally expresses the image of God.
summaries.vision-biblical: A vision in Scripture is a divinely given seeing — an unveiling of what is otherwise hidden, granted by God to His prophet, apostle, or appointed seer.
summaries.vivification: Vivification is the Spirit's active work of making alive, renewing, and enlivening the believer's inner man — the positive counterpart to mortification.
summaries.vocation: Vocation is God's purposeful calling upon a person's life — both to salvation and to specific works and roles He has ordained for them.
summaries.voice-god: The Scripture's image for God's authoritative self-revelation, both audible-historical (at Sinai, baptism, transfiguration) and ongoing (through Scripture and the Spirit's…
summaries.voluntarism: Theological voluntarism affirms that God's will is sovereign and ultimate. "Our God is in the heavens; he does all that he pleases" (Psalm 115:3).
summaries.votum: The Votum (Latin "vow") is the opening declaration of dependence in classical Reformed worship: "Our help is in the name of the LORD, who made heaven and earth" (Psalm 124:8).

summaries.vow: A vow is a solemn, binding promise made to God. Unlike casual promises between people, biblical vows invoke the name and character of God as witness and guarantor.
summaries.vows: Solemn voluntary promises made to God, often in the context of distress or thanksgiving, binding once made.
summaries.vulnerability: Vulnerability, biblically understood, is honest exposure of weakness, sin, and need before God and trusted brothers.
summaries.wack: Dismissive Gen-X-era slang for something judged bad, weak, or uncool. The slang frames taste as moral category — what is wack is to be rejected.
summaries.wage-biblical: Wage is what is owed the worker in exchange for labor — an obligation Scripture takes with the highest seriousness. Paul: the labourer is worthy of his reward (1 Tim 5:18).
summaries.wages-justice: God's requirement that workers be paid promptly and fairly.
summaries.wail: Wailing is audible, unrestrained, communal grief — the sound of a culture that knows how to mourn. Ancient Near Eastern funerals included professional wailers;
summaries.wait-on-lord: To wait on the LORD is active, hopeful expectation — not passive inaction. "Those who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles;
summaries.wait-on-yhwh: To "wait on the LORD" is the disciplined posture of expectant trust — not passive idleness but active, hope-laden patience.
summaries.waiter: A waiter in Scripture is a servant who waits at table or attends a master — an honorable role, not a humble one.
summaries.waiting: The discipline of active, hopeful expectancy that defers self-rescue and trusts God's timing.
summaries.walk-biblical: To walk in Scripture is to live — the step-by-step journey of obedience, relationship, and direction. "Enoch walked with God, and he was not, for God took him" (Gen 5:24).
summaries.walk-spirit: Paul's command for the entire Christian life. Galatians 5:16: This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.
summaries.walk: To walk, in Scripture, is the dominant metaphor for the conduct of life — the continuous pattern of behavior, choices, and direction. "To walk" is to live one’s daily way.
summaries.walking-on-water: Walking on water is one of the most iconic miracles of Jesus, and one of the most theologically loaded.
summaries.walking-water: Following the feeding of the five thousand, the disciples crossed the Sea of Galilee in a boat in a storm.
summaries.walking-with-god: Walking with God is the most comprehensive biblical description of the godly life. It is not first a theology or a set of practices; it is a companionship.
summaries.walls-jericho: The first conquest-city of the Canaan campaign. By YHWH's command, Israel marched around Jericho's walls once daily for six days, and seven times on the seventh day;
summaries.wander: Wandering in Scripture carries both physical and theological weight. Israel's forty years in the wilderness were not mere geography —
summaries.warfare: Biblical warfare operates on two inseparable levels: physical and spiritual.
summaries.warrior-prayer: The biblical pattern of prayer as warfare against spiritual enemies.
summaries.warrior: The biblical warrior is a man whose strength is submitted to God's cause.
summaries.washing-feet: The act Christ performed at the Last Supper, washing the feet of His twelve disciples — including Judas — with a basin and towel (John 13).
summaries.watch-and-pray: Watch and pray is Christ's command to the disciples in Gethsemane: watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak.
summaries.watch-biblical: "Watch" is Jesus' most repeated imperative about His return. "Watch therefore, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming" (Matt 24:42). "Be on guard, keep awake.
summaries.watchful: Watchful is the disposition of alertness — observant, on guard.
summaries.watchfulness: Watchfulness is the posture of the faithful believer who takes seriously both the reality of spiritual danger and the promise of Christ's return.
summaries.watching: Watching is the discipline of spiritual alertness — staying awake to the Lord’s return, to the soul’s drift, and to the enemy’s schemes —
summaries.watchman-roles: The watchman's roles are three: to perceive (see what is coming), to warn (sound the trumpet so the people can prepare), and to intercede (cry to God on their behalf).
summaries.watchman: A sentinel appointed by God to stand at the spiritual frontier of a people and warn them of coming danger — whether enemy attack, divine judgment, or encroaching false teaching.
summaries.watchstand: A watchstand is the fixed post at which a sentry is posted — the spot from which he is responsible to perceive and report.
summaries.watchtower: The watchtower is the station of the biblical watchman. Isaiah sits on his watchtower awaiting the vision (Isa 21:6-12);
summaries.watchword: A watchword is the password a sentry uses to distinguish friend from foe in the dark. Scripture has its watchwords: Hear, O Israel; the LORD our God is one LORD (the Shema);
summaries.water-from-rock: The water-from-the-rock was the wilderness miracle of YHWH providing water from a stone when Israel was dying of thirst.
summaries.water-motif: The Water Motif runs from Eden's four rivers (Gen 2:10-14) through the Flood, Israel's sea-crossing, the rock's waters in the wilderness (Ex 17, Num 20), the temple stream (Ezek…
summaries.water-rock: God's miraculous provision for Israel in the wilderness, and a typological picture of Christ.
summaries.water-wine: Christ's first sign in John's Gospel (John 2:1-11), performed at the wedding at Cana of Galilee.
summaries.water: Water in Scripture is never merely H₂O. It functions as a comprehensive symbol across the whole biblical narrative. In Genesis 1, the Spirit hovers over the waters —
summaries.wave-offering: The wave offering (tenuphah) was a ceremonial act in which portions of a sacrifice were waved before the LORD as a symbolic presentation and dedication.
summaries.waving-palms: Waving palms is the gesture of greeting a king, a deliverer, or a triumphant warrior — and Scripture loads it with messianic significance.
summaries.way-truth-life: Christ's threefold predicate-claim in John 14:6: "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
summaries.weakness-biblical: Paul's most distinctive teaching: weakness is the condition for divine power. "My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness...
summaries.weakness-strength: The biblical pattern of weakness becoming strength: 2 Cor 12:9-10 ("My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness...
summaries.weakness: Weakness is the state Paul learned to glory in — not endorsed sin or moral failure, but the human limitation that drives a man to depend on Christ.
summaries.weariness-good: "Weariness in well-doing" names the temptation, especially upon long-faithful saints, to grow tired of doing right when fruit seems slow and reward delayed.
summaries.wedding-banquet: Christ's parable in Matthew 22:1-14. A king prepares a wedding feast for his son and sends servants to call the invited guests. They refuse, abuse the servants, and kill some.
summaries.wedding-feast: A wedding feast is the covenant celebration meal at the marriage of two parties. Christ began His public ministry at the wedding at Cana (Jn 2), turning water into wine;
summaries.weep: To weep in Scripture is to grieve audibly, bodily, unrestrained by propriety. The Bible does not trim its weeping.
summaries.weeping: The shedding of tears, often audibly; in Scripture, used for grief, repentance, intercession, and even joy. Hannah wept and prayed; David wept until exhausted in Ziklag;
summaries.well: A well is a hollow shaft sunk into the earth to reach water — a daily necessity in the ancient Near East, and in Scripture also a recurring setting of covenant meetings.

summaries.wheat-and-tares: Christ's parable about the kingdom of heaven: a man sows good seed in his field;
summaries.wheat-tares: Christ's parable in Matthew 13:24-30, interpreted by Christ Himself in 13:36-43. A man sows wheat in his field;
summaries.wheat: Wheat is the Bible's picture of genuine fruit — the grain God gathers into His barn versus the chaff or tares fit only for burning.
summaries.white-biblical: White is Scripture's color of purification and glory. "Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow" (Isa 1:18).
summaries.white-horse: Two distinct white horses in Revelation. (1) The first of the four horsemen (Rev 6:2) on a white horse with a bow and a crown, going forth conquering and to conquer.
summaries.white-knight: A man who treats "defending women" as the highest moral category, overriding his other God-given loyalties: to Christ first, then to his own wife in covenant, then to his fellow…
summaries.white-knighting: The activity of the white knight: positioning oneself as the defender of a woman in a public dispute without first weighing the case, often against other men whom one owes deeper…
summaries.white-throne-judgment: The Great White Throne Judgment is the final judgment scene of Revelation 20:11-15. The dead, small and great, stand before the throne;
summaries.white-throne: The throne of final judgment in Revelation 20:11-15, before which the resurrected dead — small and great — stand to be judged out of the books that are opened.
summaries.whole-armor: The complete spiritual protection commanded in Ephesians 6:10-18. Paul names six pieces —
summaries.wicked-tenants: Christ's parable in Matthew 21:33-46. A householder plants a vineyard and lets it out to tenants. He sends servants to receive his fruits; the tenants beat, stone, and kill them.
summaries.wicked: Wickedness in Scripture is not merely bad behavior but a moral orientation — a disposition of the heart turned against God and His law.
summaries.wickedness: Active, willful, settled commitment to evil; the disposition (not just the act) of the unrepentant heart.
summaries.widow-care: God identifies Himself as "father of the fatherless and protector of widows" (Psalm 68:5).
summaries.widow-mite: The poor widow Christ observed in the temple treasury, contrasted with the wealthy donors.
summaries.widow-mites: Mark 12:41-44 and Luke 21:1-4 record one of Christ's most countercultural commendations.
summaries.widow-of-nain: The Widow of Nain was the unnamed widow whose only son was being carried out for burial when Jesus arrived at the village gate.
summaries.widow: The widow is Scripture's repeated test case for a society's righteousness. "Father of the fatherless and protector of widows is God in his holy habitation" (Ps 68:5).
summaries.wife: A woman covenantally joined to a man in marriage, called by God to be a helper suitable to her husband (Genesis 2:18), to love and respect him, to manage the home with wisdom, and…
summaries.wilderness-generation: The generation of Israelites who left Egypt under Moses but died in the wilderness without entering the Promised Land —
summaries.wilderness-motif: The Wilderness Motif is the recurring biblical setting of testing, refinement, and divine encounter between deliverance and inheritance. Israel's 40 years between Egypt and Canaan;
summaries.wilderness-testing: The biblical pattern of God leading His people into wilderness conditions to humble, test, and form them.
summaries.wilderness: The wilderness in Scripture is not merely a geographical location — it is a theological classroom.
summaries.wiles-of-devil: The wiles of the devil is Paul's phrase in Ephesians 6:11: put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
summaries.willow: A pliant water-loving tree of the streamside;
summaries.wine-new: Fresh wine as a biblical symbol of the Spirit, the new covenant, and eschatological joy.
summaries.wine-press: The wine press is Scripture's double-edged image of harvest joy and divine judgment. In the normal rhythm, the wine press flowed with new wine at every autumn harvest —
summaries.wine: Wine carries three simultaneous biblical weights: blessing, warning, and sacrament.
summaries.winepress: The hewn pit where grapes were trodden underfoot to release juice for wine;
summaries.winnowing-fork: The instrument of separation between wheat and chaff.
summaries.winnowing: The post-threshing agricultural process of tossing grain into the air so that wind separates the lighter chaff from the heavier kernel;
summaries.winter: Winter in Scripture is the hard season — stripped trees, shortened days, travel difficult.
summaries.wisdom-above: James 3:17's description of the wisdom that comes from God, contrasted with the earthly, sensual, devilish wisdom of the prior verses: But the wisdom that is from above is first…
summaries.wisdom-from-above: Wisdom from above is James’s sevenfold portrait of true wisdom —
summaries.wisdom: Biblical wisdom is the skill of living rightly before God — the practical understanding of how to navigate life in accordance with God's created order and His revealed will.
summaries.witchcraft: The practice of seeking, channeling, or exercising supernatural power through means other than God — familiar spirits, drugs, charms, curses, divination tools, occult rituals.
summaries.witness-bearing: Witness-bearing is the act of testifying to the truth of the gospel — who Christ is and what He has done.
summaries.witness-biblical: A witness in Scripture is one who testifies to what He has seen, heard, and known. The law required two or three witnesses to establish any matter (Deut 19:15);
summaries.witness-cloud: The saints of Hebrews 11 who surround the Christian in his race.
summaries.witness: A biblical witness is one who testifies to what they have seen, heard, and experienced — particularly to the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
summaries.woe: In Scripture, "woe" functions in two registers: (1) as a cry of personal grief and distress (e.g., Isaiah's "Woe is me!" in Isa.
summaries.woke: Scripture repeatedly commands believers to be awake, alert, and watchful — but always toward God's reality, not man's social theories.
summaries.wokeness: Wokeness is the ideological religion of the late 2010s and 2020s — a fusion of critical race theory, gender ideology, queer theory, and neo-Marxist analysis.
summaries.wolf: The wolf, in Scripture, is the predatory beast and the recurring image of false prophets, heretical teachers, and abusive shepherds who scatter and devour the flock of God.
summaries.woman-valor: The Proverbs 31 portrait of feminine strength and godliness.
summaries.woman-with-issue: The Woman with the Issue of Blood was an unnamed woman who had suffered a 12-year hemorrhage, spent all her money on physicians, and grown worse.
summaries.womb: The maternal organ where God personally forms human life;
summaries.wonder: Astonishment at what is greater than the observer; in Scripture, the disposition proper to creatures contemplating the works and Person of God.
summaries.word-became-flesh: The incarnation — the eternal Logos taking on human nature without ceasing to be God.
summaries.word-fire: God's word as a consuming, purifying force. The image is Jeremiah's: is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces (Jer 23:29).
summaries.word-of-god: The Word of God is God's active speech —
summaries.word-of-the-lord: The Word of the LORD is the active, effective speech of God — both the act of speaking and the message spoken.
summaries.word-up: Late-80s / 90s hip-hop affirmation: agreed, well said, you speak truth. Companion to the earlier-defined Gen-X Word entry.
summaries.word: The Word of God is no mere text — it is the living, active communication of the living God, carrying divine authority and power to accomplish what He sends it to do (Isaiah 55:11).
summaries.words: Words are not neutral sounds but accountable utterances.
summaries.work-biblical: Work in Scripture is activity that produces something. It is given pre-Fall (Gen 2:15: dress and keep the garden); cursed in its soil post-Fall (Gen 3:17-19, sweat and thorns);
summaries.work-cursed-blessed: Work is both cursed and blessed in Scripture: blessed as the original calling of Adam in unfallen creation (Gen 2:15); cursed in its soil and texture after the Fall (Gen 3:17-19).
summaries.work-ethic: A biblical work ethic is the disciple’s steady, honest labor done "as to the Lord, and not unto men" (Colossians 3:23-24) —
summaries.work: Purposeful labor — created good before the fall, cursed at the fall, redeemed in Christ.
summaries.workmanship-biblical: Workmanship is the visible quality of work done by a workman — what the work shows about the worker.
summaries.works-of-the-flesh: The "works of the flesh" is Paul's catalog in Galatians 5:19–21 of the characteristic outputs of human nature left to itself apart from the regenerating and sanctifying work of…
summaries.world-missions: World missions is the outward movement of the gospel from the church to unreached peoples. Jesus commanded, "Go therefore and make disciples of all nations" (Matthew 28:19).
summaries.worldliness: Worldliness is the disposition or pattern of being shaped by the present evil age rather than the kingdom. Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world.
summaries.worldview: A biblical worldview begins with God as Creator, Sustainer, and Redeemer of all things. It answers the fundamental questions of existence: Where did we come from? (Creation.
summaries.wormwood: Wormwood is a bitter aromatic shrub of the wilderness (Artemisia absinthium) —
summaries.worship-spirit-truth: Christ's teaching to the Samaritan woman at the well: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth (John 4:24).
summaries.worship: Worship is the whole-person response of a creature to the Creator — ascribing to God His infinite worth through reverence, adoration, obedience, and sacrifice.
summaries.worthy-lamb: The heavenly anthem of Revelation 5:12: Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.
summaries.worthy: Having sufficient value, merit, or standing to receive honor, trust, or a position. In Scripture, "worthy" functions in two crucial directions.
summaries.wrath-lamb: The fierce judgment of Christ in Revelation.
summaries.wrath-of-god: The wrath of God is His holy, righteous, and settled indignation against all sin and unrighteousness.
summaries.wrath: The wrath of God is His holy, righteous, and settled indignation against sin and unrighteousness.
summaries.wreckage: Scripture does not euphemize the destruction that sin causes.
summaries.yahweh-yireh: Yahweh Yireh (KJV: Jehovah-jireh) is the name Abraham gave Mount Moriah after God provided a ram in place of Isaac.
summaries.yahweh: The covenant, personal, self-existent name of the God of Israel; revealed at the burning bush as I AM THAT I AM; bound to the redemption of His people from Egypt;
summaries.yapping: Talking excessively, often dismissively used to label someone whose speech is unwelcome or whose point you do not want to engage.
summaries.year-of-jubilee: The Year of Jubilee was the fiftieth year of Israel’s calendar — every seventh sabbath-year, the year after the seven-times-seventh —
summaries.yearn: To yearn is to long deeply, ache, be moved with strong desire — most often in Scripture of one heart toward another.
summaries.yearning: Yearning is the deep, often physical, almost involuntary longing of one heart for another — a parent for a lost child, a lover for a beloved, a saint for the presence of God.
summaries.yes-and-amen: "Yes and amen" is Paul’s phrase for the absolute reliability of every promise of God in Jesus Christ: "For all the promises of God in him are yea, and in him Amen, unto the glory…
summaries.yeshuah: Yeshuah (יְשׁוּעָה) is the Hebrew word for salvation — concrete and active deliverance from real enemies, real disease, real captivity, and ultimately from sin.
summaries.yhwh-jireh: The covenant name Abraham gave to Mount Moriah after God provided the ram in Isaac's place: "The LORD will provide.
summaries.yhwh-mekaddishkem: YHWH-Mekaddishkem (יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם) — "the LORD that doth sanctify you" —
summaries.yhwh-name: The Tetragrammaton, the four-letter personal covenant name of God revealed to Moses at the burning bush (Ex 3:14-15). Likely vocalized Yahweh (or Jehovah in older transliterations).
summaries.yhwh-nissi: YHWH-Nissi (יְהוָה נִסִּי) — "the LORD is my banner" — is the covenant name Moses gave the altar he built after Israel’s victory over Amalek at Rephidim (Exodus 17:14-16).
summaries.yhwh-rapha: YHWH-Rapha (יְהוָה רֹפְאֶךָ) — "the LORD that healeth thee" —
summaries.yhwh-roi: YHWH-Roi (יְהוָה רֹעִי) — "the LORD my Shepherd" — is David’s covenant name for YHWH in the most beloved psalm in the world: "The LORD is my shepherd;
summaries.yhwh-tsabaoth: YHWH-Tsabaoth (יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת) — "the LORD of hosts," "LORD of armies" —
summaries.yhwh: YHWH is the Hebrew Tetragrammaton (four-letter name) of God, revealed to Moses at the burning bush (Ex 3:14-15). Its meaning is rooted in I AM: I AM THAT I AM...
summaries.yielded: Surrendered, presented, handed-over — Paul's central language for the believer's self-offering to God.
summaries.yielding-spirit: A yielding spirit is the settled inner posture of giving way to God — not breaking, but bending; not surrendering ground to evil, but surrendering self-will to the LORD.
summaries.yirah: Yirah (יִרְאָה) is the Hebrew word for fear — especially "the fear of the LORD." It is not anxious dread or terrified flight;
summaries.yoke-easy: Christ's invitation in Matthew 11:28-30: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me;
summaries.yoke-fellow: A fellow-laborer joined under the same yoke of ministry.
summaries.yoke: The yoke in Scripture runs from bondage to blessing. Egyptian bondage was a yoke (Lev 26:13). Jeremiah wore an actual wooden yoke to symbolize Babylon's coming dominion (Jer 27-28).
summaries.yokefellow: A yokefellow is one who labors under the same yoke as another — the partner pulling the load alongside, sharing the discipline, the pace, and the weight.
summaries.yoking-unbelievers: The NT prohibition against entering covenantal partnership with unbelievers —
summaries.yore: An archaic English adverb meaning long ago, in olden times. Appears in older English translations (and once in the KJV preface) but not directly in the KJV text;
summaries.young-man-mark: The Young Man in Mark 14 was an unnamed young man who, when the soldiers seized Jesus in Gethsemane, was following at a distance with only a linen cloth around him.
summaries.young-women: "Young women" is the category Paul commits to the older women’s care in Titus 2:4-5.
summaries.youthful-lust: Paul's warning to Timothy: Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on the Lord out of a pure heart (2 Tim 2:22).
summaries.youthful: Youthful, in Scripture, names what pertains to youth — used both joyfully and warningly. Joyfully: "Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth;
summaries.zacchaeus-tree: Luke 19:1-10 records the conversion of Zacchaeus, the chief tax collector of Jericho. He was rich and despised.
summaries.zacchaeus: Zacchaeus was the chief tax collector in Jericho — wealthy, powerful, and despised by his fellow Jews as a collaborator with Rome and a cheat.
summaries.zeal-godly: Godly zeal is the Spirit-wrought ardor that consumes the saint with passion for God’s glory, His house, His name, and His people.
summaries.zeal-house: Consuming passion for God's dwelling and honor. Psalm 69:9: for the zeal of thine house hath eaten me up.
summaries.zeal: Burning intensity and passionate commitment to God, His honor, His Word, and His purposes — a fervor of the soul that refuses to be indifferent.
summaries.zealot-biblical: Scripture presents zeal in both positive and negative lights. Positively, God Himself is zealous: "The zeal of the LORD of hosts will do this" (Isaiah 9:7).
summaries.zealot: A member of the Jewish revolutionary party of the first century AD that advocated armed resistance against Rome and against the Herodians;
summaries.zealots: The Zealots were the most militant Jewish faction of the first century.
summaries.zealous-jealousy: Zealous jealousy is the burning, possessive love God Himself confesses for His people — the fire that will not share the bride with another.
summaries.zebach-offering: The zebach (זֶבַח) is the Mosaic peace offering, prescribed in Leviticus 3 — also called the "fellowship offering.
summaries.zechariah-book: A post-exilic apocalyptic-prophetic book whose night visions and messianic oracles point to the coming of Christ as humble King, pierced Shepherd, and returning Lord on the Mount…
summaries.zechariah: Post-exilic prophet (active c. 520 BC), contemporary of Haggai, son of Berechiah, son of Iddo (Zech 1:1).
summaries.zedekiah: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah (c. 597-586 BC), placed on the throne by Nebuchadnezzar as a vassal after Jehoiachin was deported.
summaries.zelophehad-daughters: Zelophehad's daughters — Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah — were five sisters whose father died in the wilderness without sons.
summaries.zenas: Zenas was a believer in the early church whom Paul commended to Titus: "Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, that nothing be wanting unto them" (Titus…
summaries.zephaniah-prophet: Late 7th century BC prophet during Josiah's reign in Judah (~640-609 BC). Three-chapter book of judgment-and-restoration.
summaries.zephaniah: The ninth of the twelve Minor Prophets, a three-chapter prophecy proclaiming the Day of the LORD as universal judgment that purifies a humble remnant.
summaries.zera: The Hebrew word for seed, with a vast biblical sweep: the seed of the woman who would crush the serpent's head (Gen 3:15), the seed of Abraham through whom nations would be…
summaries.zerubbabel: Zerubbabel is the post-exilic governor of Judah who led the first return from Babylon and laid the foundation of the Second Temple.
summaries.ziklag: Ziklag is the Philistine town King Achish gave the fugitive David as a base of operation during his years in the wilderness.
summaries.zion-worship: Zion worship is the worship that ascended from the appointed mountain — the place where God set His Name, where the temple stood, and from which the Psalms came.
summaries.zion: Zion is the Bible's most theologically layered place-name.
summaries.zophar: The third and harshest of Job's three friends, a Naamathite (Job 2:11; 11:1; 20:1).
